It runs automatically after each scan; a normal scan processes photos added since the last successful run started, plus every photo whose position has no place name looked up for it yet (its GPS changed in the file, or an earlier lookup failed; a position where the provider found no place, such as open sea, is not asked again until it changes), while a full scan goes over every photo. A photo whose place was already looked up for its position is skipped either way, so switching the Map provider renames nothing; Look up place names does. It looks up the position LibrePhotos has stored, which the scan keeps in line with the file unless you set the location yourself. A run that was cancelled or failed before it reached every photo does not count as successful.

Looks for faces in your photos and saves them. It runs automatically after each scan and looks at every photo whose faces have not been looked for yet: new photos, photos whose file was replaced, and photos the face recognition service failed on last time, for example because it was restarting or ran out of memory. Each such failure is listed in the job's errors, and the photo is tried again on the next run. A picture the service cannot read at all is listed once and not tried again. When the service cannot be reached for 20 photos in a row, the job stops with the error "Face service unreachable" and the remaining photos wait for the next run. Rescan faces looks at every photo again. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, a face recognition error counted as "no faces in this photo", the job reported no error, and only Rescan faces found those faces later. If the face recognition service had trouble while your library was scanned, run Rescan faces once after updating.

Computes the numeric encoding for faces that have been detected but not yet encoded, so they can be grouped and matched. It runs automatically as part of Scan faces. If no faces are waiting to be encoded it finishes immediately, so you may not always see a row for it. New in 1.5.1 A face region the face model finds no face in (often one imported from your files) is not a failure: the job counts it as unmatched, keeps it as a person tag without an encoding, and leaves it alone on later runs until the Face recognition model site setting changes or you press Try again on the processing status. Up to 1.5.0 each run asked again and counted every such region as a failed item, so a library with many of them showed the job as failed, and the job list did not say why.

Clusters the faces into known and unknown groups. New in 1.5.0 Uploads start it too, once enough new faces came in: at least 20, and at least 2% of all your faces. So that it does not renumber the "Unknown" groups while you work through them, it waits until 30 minutes after your last upload and 15 minutes after you last labelled, deleted or restored a face, runs at most once an hour, and waits while a scan, a face scan, Train faces or an upload of yours is still running. Any run, also one a scan or the Train button started, counts as the last one. Up to 1.4.0, faces of uploaded photos stayed among the unknown faces until you trained by hand.
This downloads the needed machine learning models to data/protected_media/data_models/.
Packs a multi-photo download into a zip file in the background. It starts when you select several photos and choose to download them, and the app offers you the file once the job finishes.

Runs after each scan to fix RAW files that were scanned as their own photos. For each photo whose main file is a RAW file, it either merges it into the matching image photo (such as a JPEG or HEIC) in the same folder and removes the leftover RAW-only entry, or — if an image file is already attached — promotes that image to be the main file. It does not re-pair Live Photo videos that were scanned separately; those are only paired during a scan. See Stacks & File Variants for more details.

New in 1.5.0 Shows the photos and videos you uploaded, from the web app, the mobile app or another client, while LibrePhotos processes them: thumbnails, dates, tags, places and faces. Uploads made close together count in one job, so its progress reads "12 of 40" for all of them. It ends a few minutes after your last upload, once every upload is processed, and then starts the search and face steps described under Calculate CLIP embeddings. A photo whose processing failed is listed in the job with the file name and the step that failed. It runs next to other jobs and never keeps you from starting a scan, and it cannot be cancelled or removed while it runs. Up to 1.4.0, uploads showed no job at all.

Checks the videos that were added to your library before LibrePhotos recorded each video's colour, codec and pixel format during the scan. It runs by itself after a scan, only while such videos are left, so most scans never show it. It rebuilds the thumbnails of every HDR video, which an older version made washed out (see HDR Videos). It does the same for every video not stored as ordinary 8-bit 4:2:0, such as 10-bit clips or the 4:2:2 Motion JPEG files older cameras record, whose animated thumbnails an older version made in a form no browser plays. For each of these videos it also drops any converted copy kept from before, so the next playback converts it again. If a rebuild fails, the old thumbnail is kept. A video whose file cannot be read at the time — for example on a drive that is not mounted — is simply tried again after the next scan. Since 1.3.0. New in 1.4.0 After an update, an admin can also start it for every user's older videos with Start on the Finish the upgrade card.

Reads the text on your photos so that search can find it, and uses it to detect documents. It runs only while an administrator has selected a text recognition model: when you click Extract (or Extract text again for all photos) on the Library page, and New in 1.5.0 by itself after a scan or an upload, for the photos still without text. Up to 1.4.0 it never ran by itself. See Text Recognition.

New in 1.4.0 Started with Generate (or Generate captions again for all photos) under Captions on the Library page. Writes a generated caption for each of your photos that has none, or for every photo again; a caption you wrote yourself is never changed. It never runs by itself after a scan. See Captioning the whole library.

Groups burst sequences into stacks, using your burst detection rules. It starts when you click Detect stacks on the Organizing → Stacks page. See Stacks & File Variants. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, it was listed as Scan photos.

Finds duplicate photos in your library using perceptual hashing. It detects both exact copies (via hash comparison) and visual duplicates (via a two-pass algorithm). Results are shown in the Organizing page, where you can review and manage them; the button that starts this job there is called Detect duplicates. See Duplicate detection for more details.

Removes the photo's EXIF and XMP (GPS position, camera serial number, keywords) and a video's location from the thumbnails LibrePhotos 1.2.1 and older wrote, across every user's library. An admin starts it with Remove photo details from old thumbnails under Admin area > Admin tools; see After upgrading from 1.2.1 or older. It only rewrites thumbnails that still carry metadata, so running it again is quick and safe. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, this was only the strip_thumbnail_metadata command.

New in 1.4.0 Reads the exposure time again for the photos whose shutter speed 1.3.0 or older stored wrongly, across every user's library. It runs by itself once after updating from such a release, and shows on the Finish the upgrade card. Only that one value is read from each photo; nothing is written to your files. See After upgrading from 1.3.0 or older.

New in 1.4.0 Started with the Empty trash button on the Trash page. Permanently deletes every photo in your trash, including the original files on disk. It only touches your own photos, and a photo it cannot delete is skipped and makes the job end as failed. See Emptying the trash.

New in 1.4.0 Started with Apply under Dates on the Library page, or with Apply to existing photos on the date rules card after you saved changed rules. Reads the date of every photo of yours again with your current date rules and moves the photos whose date changed to their new day; a date you set by hand stays, and nothing is written to your files. A photo whose date cannot be read keeps its date and is listed in the job. See Applying the rules.

New in 1.4.0 Started with Write now under Write edits to files in Settings → Metadata options. Writes the edits that are only in LibrePhotos (ratings, dates and locations you set, rotations, captions, tags and face tags) to your sidecars or media files, as that setting says; a photo with nothing to write is left alone. It ends with how many photos it wrote, and lists the photos it could not write. See Writing the edits of a whole library.

New in 1.4.0 Asks the Map provider set in Site settings again for the place of every photo with a location, across every user's library, for example after switching to ExifTool. An admin starts it with Look up place names again under Admin area > Admin tools, after a confirmation. Photos move to the Places albums of their new names, and the day albums name their places again; a photo whose lookup fails keeps its old place. See Switching the provider.

New in 1.4.0 Started with Move to folder… for a selection of more than 100 photos. Moves your photos, with all their files, to another folder of your library, one photo after the other; a photo whose name is taken there is renamed or skipped as you chose. A cancel stops after the photo it is on, and the photos moved until then stay moved. It ends with how many photos moved and how many stayed where they were. See Moving photos to another folder. New in 1.5.0 With Sort into folders by date each photo goes into the folder of its capture date, and photos without a date are counted as staying.

New in 1.5.0 Deletes the faces that were saved twice on the same photo, across every user's library: where two faces of a photo overlap, the one with a name stays (the older one, when both or neither have a name). An admin starts it with Remove duplicate faces under Admin area > Admin tools, after a confirmation; the deleted duplicates do not go to the Deleted tab and cannot be restored. It ends with how many photos it checked and how many faces it deleted. The same work runs from the command line, for every user or one: docker compose exec backend python manage.py deduplicate_faces docker compose exec backend python manage.py deduplicate_faces --user anna --chunk-size 200 --chunk-size (default 500) is how many photos are compared at a time. Up to 1.4.0, only the Deduplicate faces action on selected photos in the Django admin did this.

New in 1.5.0 Gives the videos added before 1.5.0 the still picture the photo grid shows until you point at a video, across every user's library. It runs by itself once after the update and shows on the Finish the upgrade card. Each picture is made from the video's big thumbnail, so it is quick and no video is decoded or changed. A video without a big thumbnail is skipped, and one whose picture cannot be made is listed in the job; both keep playing their clip in the grid as before. See Video previews in the grid.

New in 1.5.0 Reads every file of every user's library again and compares it with what LibrePhotos has, to find files that were replaced while keeping their old modification date (cp -p, rsync --times, some sync apps), which a scan does not notice. An admin starts it with Check file contents under Admin area > Admin tools, for all users or one user and, optionally, one folder of that user's library; the rehash_files command does the same. A changed file is imported again as a scan would (see Files replaced in place), and the photos holding it are then read again by a scan of their owner's. The job's page shows how many files were read, what became of the changed ones, per user, and the files that could not be read. It reads every byte, so it takes hours on a large library, and other jobs wait until it finishes.

New in 1.5.0 Started with Rename files… for a selection of more than 100 photos. Gives your photos, with all their files, the name made from their capture date, one photo after the other; a taken name gets (1), (2). A cancel stops after the photo it is on, and the photos renamed until then keep their new names. It ends with how many photos were renamed, how many kept their names, and how many could not be renamed (their files keep their old names). See Renaming photos by their date.

New in 1.5.1 Some apps turn a photo's pixels when they export it but keep the face tags they wrote for the picture before the turn. Up to 1.5.0, LibrePhotos put such a face a quarter turn away from the face: it never got an encoding, and Scan faces found the face again as a second face without a name. This job moves those faces onto the face, across every user's library. An admin starts it from the Finish the upgrade card. A face is moved only when exactly one of the two quarter turns lands on a face LibrePhotos found on the photo, and that face has no name or the same name. The face then takes that face's place and encoding, and the copy is deleted; it does not go to the Deleted tab. Anything else stays as it is, for example a face found there that you named as someone else. Your files are not changed, and the photo's faces are not looked for again. It ends with how many faces it repaired and how many it left. The same work runs from the command line; --dry-run only counts the faces: docker compose exec backend python manage.py repair_turned_faces --dry-run docker compose exec backend python manage.py repair_turned_faces

When you are logged in as an admin, click on the profile picture in the top right corner and then navigate to Admin area. You should see the jobs at the bottom of the page in a table called Worker logs. Click a row in the Worker logs table to open that job's detail page. It shows the job's ID and status, when it was queued, started and finished, how long it ran, who started it, and the current progress step. If the job failed, an Error Details section shows the captured error message and the full result data. The page has the same Cancel (while the job is unfinished) and Remove buttons as its row, with the same confirmation; after Remove it goes back to the list. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, the detail page had neither button.
documents.s: Where to get information about previous run jobs

documents.t: LibrePhotos checks every hour for jobs that have made no progress for a day and marks them failed, with the error "Job made no progress for 24 hours"; the job keeps the errors it had recorded. A job that runs for days but keeps making progress, such as the first scan of a large library, is left alone. The threshold is the STUCK_JOB_HOURS variable (see Environment variables). New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, every job was marked failed 24 hours after it started, even while it was still working. New in 1.5.0 A job that a running worker is still busy with is left alone too, however long it goes without progress: Find similar faces reports none while it groups the faces of a large library. Up to 1.4.0, such a job could be marked failed while it worked, and still showed as failed after it succeeded. Not released yet (comes after 1.6.0) So is a job whose work still waits in the queue, for example behind another user's scan of a large library: it starts in its turn. Up to 1.6.0, such a job was marked failed after a day of waiting and then did nothing when its turn came. Not released yet (comes after 1.6.0) A job now always runs exactly the photos it counted when it started, and reaches 100 % with the last of them. Photos that need the work only after it started wait for the next run. Up to 1.6.0, a job could stop short of 100 % when another job did some of its photos meanwhile (it then counted as running for a day and held up the next start), or reach 100 % and start its follow-up jobs before all of its photos were done. Work that runs again after a restart is no longer counted twice either. Not released yet (comes after 1.6.0) Some jobs cover the whole server rather than one user's library: Look up place names, Check file contents, Download models and the upgrade tasks (such as Remove photo details from thumbnails). Only one of each runs at a time, whichever admin starts it; a second start answers that the job is already running. A scan does not start while a move or rename of your photos is running, just as a move waits for a scan; a move or rename of a few photos done at once shows in the job list as a short Move photos or Rename photos job for that reason. A job waiting its turn in the queue counts as running however long it waits, so the same job is not started twice meanwhile. Up to 1.6.0, two admins could run the same server-wide job side by side, and a scan could start in the middle of a move. New in 1.5.0 When LibrePhotos restarts while jobs run (an update, a changed compose file, a reboot, a worker killed for using too much memory), the work the old backend had already taken from the queue runs again about 10 minutes after the restart. A scan interrupted that way still reaches 100 % and starts its follow-up jobs. Up to 1.4.0, that work stayed in the queue for months: the scan stopped just short of 100 %, was marked failed a day later and never started its follow-ups. If a job is still running and you want to stop it, use the Cancel button in its Worker logs row or on its detail page, or the one under the progress bar in the account menu. A dialog asks first; Keep running leaves the job alone. Cancelling marks the job as cancelled and finished and removes any of its steps that are still waiting in the queue. Jobs check for cancellation as they go and stop at their next checkpoint, so it can take a few seconds before a running job actually stops; photos a scan already took off the queue are skipped. A model download or a download of selected photos still runs to the end. Find similar faces is the one exception while it rebuilds the face clusters: it finishes the rebuild, so you are not left without clusters, but it does not start Train faces afterwards. Cancelling frees the queue for a new job at once, so you do not need to remove the entry afterwards. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, a cancelled scan kept importing the photos it had queued, and duplicate and stack detection, face training, search embeddings, file variant repair and event albums ran to the end. The next scan picks up what a cancelled or failed scan, tagging, geolocation or face scan left behind. The Remove button only deletes the log entry from the database — it does not stop a running job. Use it for a job that has genuinely crashed (nothing is progressing and the logs show an ungraceful failure) so that the queue will accept new jobs again. Removing a finished job deletes its record and result; nothing in your library changes. Two runs are different, because a later run starts from them: The newest scan of the whole scan directory that reached every file is the reference for the next normal scan, which only rereads the files changed since then (see Scan photos). Without it, the next normal scan reads every file of your library again, as a full scan does. So its Remove button is greyed out, and pointing at it says "This scan is the reference for the next incremental scan"; LibrePhotos refuses to remove it in any other way too, also for an admin. It can be removed once a newer scan of the whole library has finished. A cancelled scan, a scan of a few selected files or a Nextcloud scan does not replace it. This scan is kept by the automatic cleanup of old jobs as well. The newest complete Add geolocation run: the next one looks up the photos added since it started. Remove it and the next run looks up the places of every photo added since the run before it, or of all your photos if none is left. The confirmation dialog warns about it. New in 1.6.0 To clear a long list at once, open Account menu > My jobs and click Remove finished jobs. A dialog says how many jobs go. It removes the records of your finished jobs, whether they completed, failed or were cancelled. It keeps a job that is still running or queued, the scan the next normal scan is measured against, and every Add geolocation run that went through all its photos, so nothing in your library changes and the next scans work as before. The button is greyed out, with the reason, when there is nothing to remove. It is not on the Worker logs table of the Admin area, which lists every user's jobs; remove those one at a time. Up to 1.5.1, My jobs could only remove one job per click. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, the reference scan could be removed, and the next scan then read the whole library again. The confirmation dialog could not tell which scan was the reference, and it also warned about Scan faces, which picks the photos whose faces have not been looked for whatever ran before. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, Cancel and Remove acted on the first click, without asking.
documents.s: What to do when a job gets stuck

documents.t: The Library page is your central hub for managing your photo library. Open it with Account menu > Library (on a phone, tap your picture at the right end of the bottom bar), or via the spotlight search (Ctrl+K → "Library"). View statistics at the top right of the page opens the Statistics charts.

At the top of the Library page, you'll see quick stats about your library: Photos — Total number of photos and the number of distinct days they were taken on (undated photos are grouped into a single extra bucket) People — Number of recognized people and of all faces detected; hover for a breakdown of inferred, labeled, and unknown faces Events — Number of events (photos grouped by when they were taken) Places — Number of places your photos were taken in

New in 1.5.0 After a scan or an upload, LibrePhotos keeps working on the new photos for a while: it makes their thumbnails, finds the things in them, gets them ready for search, looks up their places and finds the faces. The Processing status card under the overview stats says how far it got, one row per stage that is turned on. Photos in the trash and missing photos are not counted. Stage What is left Thumbnails Photos without a thumbnail, or whose thumbnail has no size yet; such photos show a grey square or are missing from the timeline. Run now reads their files again (as a rescan), and so does the next Scan. Things Photos not checked for things yet (only while Things are on). Search Photos without search data for the current search model. Places Photos with a GPS position whose place name was not looked up yet (only while reverse geocoding is on). Face detection Photos not checked for faces yet (only while face detection is on). Face recognition data Faces that cannot be grouped into people yet. Run now prepares them and, while face grouping is on, groups them. Text in photos Photos the selected text recognition model has not read yet. A photo it failed on three times is left out; Extract on the Library page tries it again. Captions Photos without a generated caption (only while captions are on). The header says how many stages are done. Run now starts the job that does what is left of that stage, for your photos only: the same job the scan runs afterwards, never one that starts over. While the stage's job runs, its row shows the progress and a View job link instead. When the last run of a stage could not process some photos, the row says how many and links to the job list, where the job lists them. Like every job button, Run now waits while another job runs. When every stage is done, the card is a single line, "All N photos are processed"; Show details opens the rows again. A library without photos has no card. New in 1.5.1 A face region imported from your files where the face model finds no face (or a box you drew around something it does not see as a face) stays a person tag without recognition data, so it is never grouped with a stranger. Face recognition data does not count such regions as left to do: the row says "N face regions have no face match (kept as person tags)", also on the single line when everything else is done. LibrePhotos does not ask the face model about them again until an admin picks another Face recognition model in the site settings or you press Try again next to that line, which asks once more and then runs the stage. Up to 1.5.0 they counted as left to do forever, every run asked again, and with enough of them the job showed as failed. If your photos only come from uploads (you have no scan directory), photos uploaded before LibrePhotos 1.4.0 that have no faces count as not checked for faces until a face scan has looked at them once: press Run now on Face detection. The row says so. For scripts: the card reads GET /api/library/processing-status/, and Run now is POST /api/library/processing-status/run/ with the stage's key, for example {"stage": "places"} (keys: thumbnails, things, search, places, face_detection, face_recognition, text, captions). A stage that is off is a 403; its job already running is a 409 that names the job.

In the Scan library row, click Scan to scan your configured scan directory for new photos. The scan process: Discovers new image and video files Groups related files (RAW+JPEG pairs, Live Photos) as file variants. A RAW and a JPEG with the same name in the same folder become one photo with a RAW variant; there is no setting for this. Creates thumbnails, and for a video a short animated preview for the grid (which can be turned off) Extracts EXIF metadata Runs face detection Detects the things in each photo with OpenCLIP, which also gives each photo its semantic-search embedding Performs reverse geocoding Calculates the search embeddings the thing detection could not The scan imports images, videos, RAW files and XMP sidecars. Any other file in your folders, such as an editor sidecar (.pp3, .aae) or Thumbs.db, is skipped and does not count as an error. The .json files of a Google Takeout export are read for the date, location and description of their photo and are not photos themselves (see Importing a Google Takeout export). New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0 they were skipped too. A file that looks like a photo or video but cannot be read, such as an empty .jpg or one whose header is damaged, is still listed in the scan job's errors (see Job System). A Scan processes new and changed files, and also every photo whose metadata could not be read last time (for example because the exif service was restarting or timed out): such a photo is listed in the job's errors, and the next scan reads it again, even though the file has not changed. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, only a Rescan read those photos again; after the update, the first Scan also reads the photos earlier scans left without metadata. New in 1.4.0 A folder LibrePhotos is not allowed to read, such as a lost+found folder owned by root or a NAS recycle bin, is skipped and the rest of the library is still scanned. The scan then finishes as a partial failure and its job lists the folder with the reason. Because the photos in that folder were not looked at, that scan does not check for missing photos. If the scan directory itself cannot be read, the scan fails. To re-process all existing photos, open the dropdown next to Scan (the chevron) and choose Rescan.

New in 1.5.0 A library can have more than one folder. The Library folders card above Photos lists them: the scan directory (marked Main folder), the further folders an admin added, and the upload folder when it lies outside them. Each row says how many of your photos are in it, and its menu (⋮) opens the folder on the Folders page. A Scan reads every folder of the library. Admins add a folder with Add folder under the list and remove one with Remove… in its menu; see Several library folders per user. Other users see their folders here and ask an admin for changes. A folder that cannot be read right now, such as one on a disk that is unplugged, shows Not found. Scans skip it and go on with the rest of the library, list it in the job's errors, and do not mark its photos missing: they come back as they were when the disk does.

New in 1.5.0 You can leave folders inside your library folders out of your library, for example the trips of a relative in a shared family folder. Choose Leave out subfolders… in a folder's menu (⋮): the dialog shows its subfolders with a checkbox each and how many of your photos are in them. Untick a folder to leave it, and everything in it, out; open a folder with the arrow to get to the folders inside it. Save applies the change to every folder at once. Scans skip the folders you left out from then on, and so do scans of chosen files and folder watchers. The row of the library folder says how many subfolders are left out. Photos already imported from those folders stay in your library until you move them to the trash: tick Also move my photos outside my library to the trash before saving. That moves every photo of yours that is outside your library folders to the trash, those in the folders you left out included; you can restore them from the trash until it is emptied. Files on disk are never touched. Moving photos into a folder you left out is refused. Tick the folder again to take it back in; the next scan imports its photos again. You cannot leave out a library folder itself (ask an admin to remove it) or a folder that holds your upload folder. Leaving folders out only changes your own library; the same folders stay in the libraries of others. Only one job runs at a time, for all users together. While one runs, the job buttons on this page are greyed out and a note above them says so: it names the job and links to the job list when it is yours (or you are an admin), and says "Another user's job is running" otherwise. New in 1.4.0 Point at or tab to a greyed-out button to see why it is unavailable. Note AI captions are not generated during a scan — they are created per photo on demand. Open a photo, show the details panel, and use the wand icon in the Caption section. See Image Captioning.

If you overwrite a file with a different picture but keep the same name, the next scan picks the change up and re-indexes it: the thumbnails are rebuilt from the new picture and the photo goes back into the queue for face detection, things and geocoding. It keeps its album membership, its sharing and its link, so anything pointing at it still works. New in 1.5.0 What LibrePhotos worked out from the old picture goes with it: its things, its generated caption, its search data and the text found in it. The jobs after that scan find the things and make the search data again from the new picture; the text and a generated caption are made again the next time Extract Text or Generate captions runs. What you entered stays: your own caption, tags, rating, albums, and a date or location you set by hand. Up to 1.4.0, the old things, caption and text stayed with the new picture. A file whose bytes changed while its picture stayed the same is only re-keyed internally. That covers a rating or a face tag LibrePhotos wrote into the original, and metadata another tool edited in place: nothing is regenerated and nothing you corrected by hand is lost. New in 1.5.0 The same goes for a picture another app saved again, compressed again or edited lightly (a slightly brighter version, say): it keeps its faces, things, caption and place in the timeline, and only its thumbnails are made again so that they show the file as it is now. Uploading such a file again is recognised as a photo you already have. Up to 1.4.0, any change to the picture's fingerprint counted as a new picture and cost the photo its faces. New in 1.5.0 A scan only reads a file again when its modification date changed. A file replaced by a copy that kept the old date (cp -p, rsync --times, some sync apps) is not noticed; an admin finds those with Check file contents in the Admin area (see Check File Contents), or with python manage.py rehash_files (--user <name> for one library, --path <folder> for one folder of it). For a video, and for a photo you have rotated inside LibrePhotos, the two cannot be told apart. The scan takes the careful path there: the thumbnails are rebuilt once and the cached video conversion is dropped, but the faces you have named are kept and the photo stays where it is in the timeline. Note The first scan after upgrading may re-key files LibrePhotos had previously written metadata into. That is bookkeeping with no visible change to your library, and it happens only once per file.

New in 1.4.0 When one photo is wrong (a bad thumbnail, a date that does not match the file after another app edited it, a file replaced with one that kept the old modification time), you can read just its files again instead of rescanning the whole library: Several photos: select them, open the ⋮ (Photo actions) and choose Rescan files in the Files group. Up to 1,000 photos at a time; after Select all, pick the photos one by one instead. One photo: in the photo viewer, open the ⋮ (More actions) at the right end of the toolbar and choose Rescan file. On the photo's page it is under More. A rescan reads every file of the photo again, also when it did not change: the main file, its variants and its sidecars. It renders the thumbnails again (the old ones stay if that fails), reads the metadata and the date, and checks the file's hash. What you changed in LibrePhotos stays: a date you set by hand, a location you set, captions and albums (see How a rescan treats your edits for every field). The things, places and faces jobs that follow only look at what is new, as after a Scan, so a rescan does not detect faces again: use Detect faces again next to it for that (see Face recognition). The items are only shown for your own photos, not for photos someone shared with you. Like every job, a rescan waits while another job runs. It is never what the next Scan compares the library against, so a file changed elsewhere in the library is still picked up then.

Scan progress is shown in the Job System. The scan is split into smaller tasks, prioritizing thumbnail creation so photos appear in the UI quickly while heavier processing (faces, things) happens in the background.

New in 1.4.0 You can move your own photos to another folder of your library without leaving LibrePhotos. Select the photos and choose Edit info → Move to folder… in the photo actions menu (⋮), or open a photo and choose More → Move to folder…. The dialog shows the folders of your library: your scan directory and, when it is set elsewhere, your upload folder. Folders the scan skips (hidden folders and the ones matching the skip patterns) are not listed, and you cannot move photos outside your library. Pick a folder in the tree or type its full path. New folder names a folder inside the one you picked; it is made when the photos move. Before you move, the dialog says how many photos and files move and which photos stay where they are: photos already in that folder; local copies of Nextcloud files, which the next Nextcloud scan would download again to the old place; photos that share a file with another photo; photos whose files are missing on disk. A photo moves with all its files: the main file, its RAW or JPEG variant, a Live Photo's video and its XMP sidecars (both IMG_1.xmp and IMG_1.jpg.xmp). It moves completely or not at all: if one file cannot be moved, the others are put back. A Motion Photo video that LibrePhotos extracted into its own data folder stays there. If a file with the same name is already in the folder, a second dialog lists the names and lets you choose: Rename, keep both: the moved photo gets a free name, such as IMG_1 (1).jpg, for all its files, so they still belong together. Skip: those photos stay where they are. A file in the folder is never overwritten. Albums, faces, tags, ratings and sharing stay with the photo, and the folder views show it in its new folder right away. The next scan does not read a moved photo again. A selection of more than 100 photos moves in the background as a Move photos job (see Job System); a move cannot start while a scan of your library runs.

New in 1.5.0 Turn on Sort into folders by date in the same dialog to give each photo a folder of its own capture date inside the destination, for example /photos/sorted/2025/06 and /photos/sorted/2025/07. Choose the folders with {year}, {year}/{month} or {year}/{month}/{day}. Missing folders are made when the photos move. The dialog lists the folders the photos go to, how many photos each one gets and where a name is taken, and shows an example path with the date folders in colour. Photos without a capture date stay where they are; Change date and time… next to their count gives them a date without leaving the dialog. Everything else works as for one folder: taken names, the photos that stay, and the job for more than 100 photos. A date folder that the scan would skip is refused.

New in 1.5.0 You can give your own photos file names made from their capture date, such as 20250601_233000.jpg instead of IMG_4711.jpg, so they are easy to find and share outside LibrePhotos. Select the photos and choose Edit info → Rename files… in the photo actions menu (⋮), or open a photo and choose More → Rename files…. Pick a preset (Date and time, Date, time and old name, Date and old name) or write your own name with these tokens; the buttons under the field put one where the cursor is: Token Becomes {year} {month} {day} the capture date, such as 2025 06 01 {hour} {minute} {second} the capture time where the photo was taken, such as 23 30 00 {name} the current file name without its extension, such as IMG_4711 The extension stays. A name cannot contain \ / : * ? " < > | or start with a dot, so a renamed file stays in its folder on every system. Before you rename, the dialog lists the first photos with a thumbnail, their name now and the name they get, and counts the rest: photos that already have the name keep it; photos without a capture date are skipped (Change date and time… gives them one); the same photos as for a move keep their names: local copies of Nextcloud files, photos that share a file with another photo, photos whose files are missing on disk. A photo is renamed with all its files, as for a move: its RAW or JPEG variant, a Live Photo's video and its XMP sidecars (IMG_1.CR2 becomes 20250601_233000.CR2, IMG_1.jpg.xmp becomes 20250601_233000.jpg.xmp), so the scan still sees one photo. When a name is taken, for example by two photos of the same second, the photo gets the next free one: 20250601_233000 (1).jpg. Nothing is ever overwritten, and a photo that cannot be renamed keeps every file under its old name. Albums, faces, tags, ratings and sharing stay with the photo. A selection of more than 100 photos is renamed in the background as a Rename photos job; a rename cannot start while a scan of your library runs.
If you have a Nextcloud instance, you can scan photos directly from it without manually transferring files.

The integration is off by default, and the Nextcloud section is hidden on the Library page until an admin turns it on. Open Account menu > Admin area → Site settings and enable the Enable Nextcloud integration switch. On a fresh install you can also pre-enable it by setting nextcloudEnabled=true in librephotos.env before the first start.

On the Library page, find the Nextcloud section Enter your Nextcloud server URL, username, and password Save your changes when the Save Changes dialog appears (click Update). The Status row at the top of the Nextcloud section then shows a green Connected badge. It reads Missing credentials, Connecting, or Disconnected while the connection is unset, in progress, or failing. Click Browse (folder icon) to select your Nextcloud photo directory A Nextcloud scan shows up as a Scan photos job that counts the new and changed files it imports. When it finishes, it starts the same follow-up jobs as a local scan: tags, places, search embeddings and faces. New in 1.5.0 Up to 1.4.0, the job showed as finished after its first photo, and the imported photos only got tags, places and faces from the next local scan.

LibrePhotos checks the certificate of an https:// Nextcloud server, and refuses a server whose certificate it does not trust. A Nextcloud with a self-signed certificate (for example the default certificate of TrueNAS) or one from your own certificate authority then shows Disconnected. LibrePhotos has no switch that turns this check off. New in 1.4.0 Instead, an admin tells it which certificate to trust: Save the certificate as a PEM file, a text file that starts with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----. Use the certificate of the authority that signed the Nextcloud certificate, or for a self-signed certificate the certificate itself. Export it from where it was made; in TrueNAS that is Credentials → Certificates. Give LibrePhotos the file and set NEXTCLOUD_CA_BUNDLE to its path, as below. Open the Library page again. The Nextcloud section now shows Connected. Docker: put the file next to docker-compose.yml, for example as certs/nextcloud-ca.pem, mount it into the backend service by adding a line to its volumes: backend: volumes: - ./certs/nextcloud-ca.pem:/certs/nextcloud-ca.pem:ro then set the path inside the container in librephotos.env and restart with docker compose up -d: nextcloudCaBundle=/certs/nextcloud-ca.pem Windows standalone: save the file anywhere on the PC, for example C:\LibrePhotos\nextcloud-ca.pem, and start LibrePhotos from a small .cmd file next to librephotos.exe that sets the variable (the same way Using another port moves a service): @echo off set NEXTCLOUD_CA_BUNDLE=C:\LibrePhotos\nextcloud-ca.pem start "" "%~dp0librephotos.exe" Things to know: The server address you enter has to be a name the certificate was made for. A certificate for nextcloud.lan is not accepted when you connect to https://192.168.1.10. With NEXTCLOUD_CA_BUNDLE set, every Nextcloud server is checked against that file only, not against the public certificate authorities. If other users of your LibrePhotos connect to a Nextcloud with a public certificate (for example from Let's Encrypt), make the file a copy of a public bundle such as /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt with your certificate added at the end. If the file is missing or holds no PEM certificate, LibrePhotos does not connect at all: the Nextcloud section shows Disconnected, and Scan answers with a message that names NEXTCLOUD_CA_BUNDLE.

In the Nextcloud section, click Scan to download and scan photos from your configured Nextcloud directory. Files are copied to the local filesystem under nextcloud_media/<username>/ before being processed. New in 1.5.0 If a download is interrupted by a connection failure, timeout or incomplete response, LibrePhotos tries it up to three times in total, waiting one second before the second attempt and two seconds before the third. Each attempt starts from the beginning. Partial downloads are removed, and an existing local copy is replaced only after the new download completes. If all three attempts fail, the scan job fails; fix the connection to Nextcloud and run Scan again. Certificate, authentication and local filesystem errors are not retried. New in 1.4.0 A repeat scan keeps the local copies in step with the server: A file that is new on the server is downloaded and imported. A file that changed on the server (it is newer or has another size) is downloaded again and processed again. An XMP sidecar that changed has its photo processed again, so ratings and keywords edited in another app arrive. A file that is unchanged is neither downloaded nor processed again. New in 1.5.0 An unchanged exact copy at another path is skipped too, rather than processing the same photo again on every scan. A file deleted on the server is flagged missing, as a file deleted from a local library is: it shows up under Remove missing photos, and the photo and the local copy stay until you remove them. If the file comes back, the next scan attaches it again. Not released yet (comes after 1.6.0) The scan flags them as its last step, after every new file was imported, so a cancelled or failed scan flags nothing, and a file moved on the server is attached at its new place before it leaves the old one. Up to 1.6.0, a scan flagged them before importing anything. A downloaded copy keeps the file's modification time on the server, so the "File modified time" date rules date it by the server's time, not by the day of the download. Copies downloaded by an older version get that time on the next scan, which processes them once more to read their date again. "Write edits to files" does not write into Nextcloud photos; see Settings. Note Nextcloud scanning indexes the same media as a local scan: images, videos, RAW files and XMP sidecars. Duplicate photos from earlier Nextcloud scans New in 1.4.0 Up to version 1.3.0, every Nextcloud scan added another copy of each photo it had already imported. The first start after upgrading merges those copies into one photo per file. The merged photo keeps the albums, tags, faces, shares and edit history of every copy and the highest rating among them; its caption, date and location come from a single copy: one that is not in the trash, preferring the copy you edited most, then the oldest.

The Library page provides quick access to common maintenance actions: Row Button Description Scan library Scan Scan for new photos in the file system Scan library (dropdown) Rescan Re-process all existing photos Generate event albums Generate Group photos into events by when they were taken Regenerate event titles Generate Regenerate the titles of existing events Train faces Train Run face clustering and classification Rescan faces Rescan Re-detect faces in all photos; for some photos or one folder see Detect faces again Nextcloud Scan Scan photos from a connected Nextcloud instance Extract Text Extract Read the text on photos that have not been read yet (see Text Recognition) Extract Text (dropdown) Extract text again for all photos Read the text on every photo again Apply date rules to existing photos Apply New in 1.4.0 Read the date of every photo again with your current date rules; a date you set by hand stays. If LibrePhotos detects photos that are no longer on disk, a red N Missing Photos badge appears next to the Photos heading. Click it to open the Remove missing photos dialog and confirm removal of those database entries. The badge is hidden when nothing is missing.

LibrePhotos runs several background ML services. Administrators can monitor and control them from the Admin area: Service Description image_similarity CLIP-based image similarity index thumbnail Thumbnail generation face_recognition Face detection and recognition image_captioning Image caption generation exif EXIF metadata extraction tags Things and semantic-search embeddings (OpenCLIP); always runs, because search needs it ocr Text recognition; only started while a Text recognition (OCR) model is selected in Site settings For each service, you can: View health status Start or stop the service; stopping asks first, because the service stops for every user of the server Services are automatically started with Django and monitored by a cron job

Administrators can download a server-stats report from the Admin area (Admin tools → Download server stats), which saves a serverstats.json file containing: CPU — Model, core count, architecture, and instruction-set flags RAM — Total system memory GPU — GPU model and memory (only populated when the container sees an NVIDIA GPU through nvidia-smi) Storage — Total, used, and free disk space Per-user stats — Detailed counts per user (photos, videos, albums, faces, and more) The stats are not rendered in the UI — download the JSON to inspect them. Per-user photo counts are also shown directly in the Admin area's user table.

A Storage card at the bottom of the sidebar shows a bar for the disk holding your LibrePhotos data directory (/data in the default Docker setup), with <used> of <total> used under it. The bar turns orange at 75% and red at 90%. It reports how full that whole volume is, so it includes the operating system and anything else on the same disk, not just your photos.

The Admin area shows a Server logs panel with the most recent log lines (1–1000, default 100) and a Refresh button. The download icon saves the full librephotos.log file (ownphotos.log in 1.3.0 and older).
The bottom of the sidebar shows the version as Version: tag (dev when IMAGE_TAG is unset), next to the Documentation and Support us links. Hover over it to see the backend git hash.

For advanced users with shell access, LibrePhotos provides several management commands: # Scan all users' photo directories (users without a scan directory are skipped) python manage.py scan # Full rescan (re-process all photos) python manage.py scan -f # Scan specific files, given by full path; each file goes to every user whose # library folders contain it (normally exactly one; /data/alice2/x.jpg is not # in /data/alice), and a file outside every library is ignored. # Since 1.5.0 a folder is scanned too, with its subfolders python manage.py scan -s /path/to/file.jpg /path/to/folder # Scan Nextcloud directories for every user that has one configured # (users without a Nextcloud scan directory are skipped; -n cannot be combined with -f or -s) python manage.py scan -n # Build similarity index for all users python manage.py build_similarity_index # Write the edits already in LibrePhotos to XMP sidecars or image files, as each # owner's "Write edits to files" setting says (users with it Off are skipped; # --sidecar or --media-file overrides it for the one user named with --user; # --types limits what is written, --dry-run only counts). The same writes as # Settings > Metadata Options > Write now. python manage.py save_metadata # Start all ML services (individual services are managed from the Admin Area) python manage.py start_service all # Clear site-wide cache python manage.py clear_cache # Back up an SQLite database into db/backups next to it and keep the newest 3 # (--keep N, or DB_BACKUP_KEEP); --if-pending-migrations only does it when # migrate has work to do. On PostgreSQL it does nothing: use pg_dump. python manage.py backup_database # Remove the original's metadata (EXIF incl. GPS, XMP, a video's location) from # thumbnails created by 1.2.1 and older; pixels and colour profiles are kept, # clean files are not touched, so it is safe to run again (--dry-run only counts) python manage.py strip_thumbnail_metadata # Read every indexed file again and import the ones whose contents changed while # their modification date stayed (cp -p, rsync --times); --user <name> for one # library, --path <folder inside it> for one folder. Reads every byte: slow. python manage.py rehash_files # Read the exposure time again where 1.3.0 and older stored the shutter speed # wrongly ("0" for anything faster than about 1/2000 s, "1/1000" for 1/1250 to # 1/2000 s, "5/2" for 2.5 s); only that tag is read (--dry-run only counts) python manage.py refresh_exposure_time # Queue the automatic tasks an update left (the Admin Area's Finish the # upgrade card), each once; the Docker image and the Windows app run it at start python manage.py start_upgrade_tasks # Create a new user (username and email are required; the password is # autogenerated unless --password is given, and --admin grants admin rights) python manage.py createuser <username> <email> # Create an admin user; the password is read from the ADMIN_PASSWORD # environment variable, otherwise a random one is generated and not printed ADMIN_PASSWORD=... python manage.py createadmin <username> <email>

Click on your Avatar → Admin area to navigate to your user panel. The user panel is at the bottom of the page above the worker logs. You can create, delete and manage users of your instance. You can change the scan path, password, name and e-mail of a given user. New in 1.5.0 The circular arrow next to a user's scan directory scans that user's library now, the same scan as the Scan button on their Library page: the job is theirs and shows in their job list. While it runs, the arrow shows its progress. So after you fix a user's scan path, you can scan it without signing in as them. On your own Library page, Change scan directories in the Admin area under Scan library leads to this table. Please note: In LibrePhotos, the file system acts as the definitive source of photo organization. This means that folder structure dictates how photos are grouped and accessed within the application. To isolate users and their photo collections, create a subfolder for each user inside the folder you set as scanDirectory in your .env file — the folder LibrePhotos mounts as /data. Inside LibrePhotos these show up as /data/user1, /data/user2, etc., and that is the path you assign as each user's scan directory. Create the folders before assigning them: LibrePhotos only accepts directories that already exist under /data. This ensures that users only see and interact with the photos in their designated directories. New in 1.5.0 You can make such a folder in the user edit dialog: choose the folder it goes in, click New folder above the folder list, type its name and press Enter. The new folder is chosen as the scan directory right away. Only admins can make folders, only inside /data, and a name cannot hold / or \, be . or .., or be a name Windows refuses (such as CON or a:b). If LibrePhotos may not write to the folder, the dialog says so; then make the folder on the host.

New in 1.5.0 When you point a user at another folder, their photos from the old folder stay theirs: nothing moves to another user. The edit dialog counts the user's photos outside the new folder and asks what to do with them before you save: Keep them in the user's library (the default): nothing changes, as before. Move them to the user's trash: after the save, a job (Trash Photos Outside the Library, shown in the job list) moves them to the user's trash. The files on disk are not touched, and the user can restore the photos from the trash until it is emptied. The Save button turns red and says how many photos it moves. Photos in the user's upload folder, in their further library folders and copies from their Nextcloud count as inside. If another user's scan directory holds the same files, that user's next scan adds them to their own library. Scan directories of different users must not overlap. Every photo belongs to exactly one user, so LibrePhotos refuses a scan directory that is the same as, inside, or above another user's scan directory, and names the user it clashes with. In particular, once one user scans /data itself, no other user can be given any folder under /data, so give every user a folder of their own, the admin included. Installations that already have overlapping scan directories keep working and those users can still be edited; only changing a scan directory to one that overlaps is refused. Two users whose scan directories overlap each get their own photo of a file both scan, with its own thumbnails and face crops. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0 the second user's photo shared an internal key with the first user's, so either of them could be refused a photo of their own or see the other's rotation of it. LibrePhotos 1.4.0 repairs those photos once while it starts, copying their thumbnails and face crops, so the first start takes a little longer and the thumbnails folder grows by those copies. If your admin account already scans /data and you want to add more users, move the admin's photos into a subfolder such as /data/admin, set that as the admin's scan directory and run a scan. The moved photos are matched to their existing entries by their content, so ratings, faces and albums are kept; see Missing Photos for how that relinking works.

New in 1.5.0 A user's library can span more than one folder, for example a folder of their own and a shared family folder, or a second disk. The scan directory stays the user's main folder (uploads go below it unless an upload folder is set); further folders are added in the user edit dialog, under Library folders: Open the user in the Admin area and click Add folder under Library folders. Pick a folder in the tree (or type its path) and click Add folder. It must already exist under /data. Run a scan: every scan reads all folders of the library from then on. The same list is on that user's Library page; as an admin you can add and remove your own folders there. Adding or removing a folder in the dialog applies right away, without Save. The rules for scan directories hold for every library folder: a folder may not be the same as, inside or above a folder of another user's library (scan directory, upload folder or a further folder), and the error names the user it clashes with. Within one library, folders may not overlap either: a folder inside the scan directory is already part of the library. A scan directory that would contain one of the user's further folders is refused until you remove that folder. Remove… in a folder's menu takes it out of the library. Its files stay on disk and its photos stay the user's, outside the library; tick Also move its photos to the user's trash to move them to the trash right after, as when the scan directory changes. The main folder cannot be removed; change the scan directory instead. A folder that cannot be read (an unplugged disk) is shown as Not found and skipped by scans; its photos are not marked missing. Every user can also leave subfolders out of their own library, from the Library page; see Leaving subfolders out. To let several users see the same photos, keep the photos in one user's library and share them from there: albums and individual photos can be shared with other users on the instance, see Sharing. Sharing photos in a family compares the setups a household can use. While the application saves metadata (e.g., tags, albums, facial recognition data) on a per-user basis in its database, it doesn’t inherently restrict access to the photos themselves. Access permissions must be managed through the file system / paths. The separation will also not keep the photos "private" as the admin of the host system can see all the images.

The red trash icon in a user's row deletes that account. Admin accounts cannot be deleted, so the icon is greyed out for them. Deleting a user removes the account, so it can no longer sign in, but it does not remove the user's library. Their photos, albums, tags and stacks stay in the database and are handed to a disabled placeholder account called deleted, which cannot sign in and is not listed in the Admin area. Nothing is removed from disk: the original files and their thumbnails stay where they are. If the photos should go as well, they have to be deleted from that user's library while the account still exists (see Trash). Since 1.3.0, deleting a user also turns off everything of theirs that people without an account could open: public album links, photo links and public photos. Those links stop working for anyone who opens them. Nobody can sign in as deleted, so nobody could turn them off later. Links left on by users deleted with an older version are turned off when you upgrade to 1.3.0. Albums and photos the user shared with other users of the instance stay shared. Those users keep seeing them, now owned by deleted. Photos that other users shared with the deleted user are taken out of the deleted user's albums, so the people those albums are shared with cannot open them later. The photos stay in their owners' libraries. A user deleted after another one can have an album or a tag with the same name as one that deleted already holds. Two albums are never mixed into one, so nobody gets to see one user's photos through the other user's shares: An album the user made gets their username added to its title, for example Holiday (bob), and keeps its photos and the users it is shared with. A generated album (an event, a day, a place or a thing) is dropped. Its photos are kept. A tag is merged into the tag of the same name. Tags are not shared with anyone.

Photos uploaded through the web interface or backed up by the mobile app are written to an uploads folder inside the user's scan directory: /data/user1/uploads/web/. The user edit dialog in the Admin area shows the folder uploads land in under the scan directory. Since 1.3.0, you can put a user's uploads somewhere else: pick a folder in the Upload folder field of the same dialog. It is checked like a scan directory: it must already exist under /data, and it must not be inside, above or the same as another user's scan directory or another user's upload folder. A folder inside the user's own scan directory is fine. Uploaded photos are scanned into the uploader's library, so an upload folder counts as part of that user's files: the same rule also refuses a scan directory that is inside, above or the same as another user's upload folder, and the error names the user and whether it clashes with their library or their upload folder. As with scan directories, a value that already overlaps is kept when you save the user without changing it. Uploads then go to <upload folder>/web/. Clear the field to go back to the default. Uploaded photos always belong to the user who uploaded them. If the upload folder is outside the user's scan directory, the photos still show up in their library, but a scan of the scan directory does not look in that folder and the folder view does not list it.

Admin area → Site settings has a Create a folder for each new user switch, off by default. With it on, creating a user — from the admin panel, from self registration, or through single sign-on — also creates /data/<username> and assigns it as that user's scan directory, so you no longer have to make the folder on the host and assign it by hand for every account. It only works when your own scan directory is a subfolder such as /data/admin, not /data itself. Scan directories of different users cannot overlap (see above), so while any user scans /data, every /data/<username> folder is refused. What it deliberately does not do: It never overwrites a scan directory you typed on the create form. An explicit path wins. It never fails account creation. If /data is read-only, the username does not name a plain folder (such as . or ..), or the folder would overlap a directory another user already scans, the account is still created — just without a scan directory — and the reason is written to the backend log. Nothing is created on disk in that case. Assign a directory by hand afterwards. It does not give a self-registered or single sign-on account a folder that already exists. Otherwise anyone who can sign up could take over, say, /data/family just by choosing family as their username. Such an account is created without a scan directory instead. When you create a user in the admin panel and /data/<username> already exists, that folder is assigned, since you can see what is in it. It does not touch existing users. Only accounts created while the switch is on get a folder.
documents.s: Giving each user their own folder automatically

documents.t: Click on your Avatar → Admin area to the user registration setting. You can also activate user registration, where user can create an account themselves. They cannot change the path, which means the admin is still in full control. Unless Create a folder for each new user is on, a self-registered account is created without a scan directory, so the new user sees an empty library and is told to contact their administrator if they try to scan or upload. After someone signs up, open the Admin area, edit their account in the user panel at the bottom of the page and set its scan path as described above.

There are three ways to accomplish that: If your .env sets the admin credentials, the password is reset every time the backend container starts. The keys are userName, userPass and adminEmail (passed to the backend as ADMIN_USERNAME, ADMIN_PASSWORD and ADMIN_EMAIL), and both the username and password must be non-empty. They are not in the shipped librephotos.env template, so add them yourself — see Admin account variables for the full behaviour. If you have access to your container, you can change the password by executing a Django management command docker exec -it [backend container name] python manage.py changepassword [admin username] If outgoing e-mail is configured on your instance, the login page shows a Forgot your password? link that e-mails a reset link to the address on your account. This only works once e-mail is set up (Admin area → Site settings → Email) and the account has an e-mail address, so arrange both before you get locked out. Behind the bundled proxy, also set frontendBaseUrl in your .env (passed to the backend as FRONTEND_BASE_URL) so the emailed link points at your public address rather than the internal one.
documents.s: How to change the admin password, when you can't log in

documents.t: Memories answers "what was I doing a year ago today?". It collects the photos you took around this date in each earlier year and lets you play them back as a slideshow. Open it with See all on the row of memories above the timeline, from Memories in the dropdown of the Photos page title, or type "memories" (or "on this day", "years ago") into the spotlight search. New in 1.6.0 To keep it one click away, pin it: Customize sidebar under the sidebar's pages, then tick Memories.

The page shows one tile per earlier year that has photos near today's date, nearest year first. Each tile carries: A cover photo — a favourite from that day if there is one, otherwise the earliest still photo. Videos are never used as covers. ("Favourite" here means the rating threshold set by Minimum image rating to interpret as favorite in Settings.) How long ago it was — "1 year ago", "4 years ago". The exact day and, when reverse geocoding has filled it in, where you were — for example Jul 14, 2022 · Lisbon. How many photos that memory holds. Clicking a tile plays that year as a slideshow. Play all at the top plays every year in a row, oldest year first, in the order the photos were taken.

The header has a Tiles / Gallery switch: Tiles (the default) shows one cover per year — a quick overview. Gallery shows all the photos from every memory in the normal photo grid, so you can select, favourite, share or add them to an album exactly as you would anywhere else. Switching to Gallery, or pressing Play all, fetches the full set of photos; the tiles view only needs the covers, so it stays fast on large libraries. Note A memory returns at most 200 photos per year. If a day of yours is bigger than that, the count on the tile still shows the true total and the page notes that it is showing the first 200 photos of each year.

A memory is built from the days your timeline already groups photos under, so a memory always covers exactly the days the timeline shows. The window. An exact "on this day" match is empty on most days for most libraries, so a memory covers the anniversary plus or minus 3 days. A weekend trip stays together without pulling in an unrelated week. The month fallback. If no year has anything in that window, the page widens to whole months instead and shows "August 2019"-style tiles. Better a memory of the right month than an empty page. This year is excluded. Photos from this year's anniversary are still near the top of your timeline, so they are not a memory yet. 29 February falls back to the 28th in years that do not have one. Your day, not the server's. The anniversary is taken from your own timezone (Settings → Metadata options → Default timezone), so memories roll over at your midnight rather than the server's.

Memories draw from the same photos your timeline shows — your own photos, not hidden, not archived, not in the trash, and only the primary photo of a stack so a RAW/JPEG pair is not shown twice. On top of that, photos detected as screenshots and documents are skipped: a screenshot from four years ago is not a memory of anything. Place names come from reverse geocoding. If you have not run Add geolocation, tiles simply show no place — see Places.

Playing a memory opens the normal lightbox already in slideshow mode, so everything you know from there still works: the interval dropdown (3, 5, 10, 15 or 30 seconds, defaulting to your Settings → Interface → Default slideshow interval), s to stop and start, arrow keys to step through by hand, g for fullscreen and Esc to close. Picking a different memory always starts its slideshow from the beginning.

If you see "No memories yet", your library does not yet reach back more than a year from today — memories only look at earlier years. This is expected on a freshly scanned library of recent photos. It also appears if every candidate photo was filtered out, for example a day that holds nothing but screenshots. Nothing needs to be generated or scheduled: memories are computed when you open the page, so newly scanned photos show up immediately.

Missing photos are photos whose metadata and thumbnails exist in LibrePhotos' database, but the actual image files cannot be found on your file system. This typically happens in two situations: Files moved or renamed externally - When you move or rename files using a file manager, operating system tools, or other programs outside of LibrePhotos Storage or mounting issues - When external drives aren't mounted, network storage is disconnected, or Docker mount points are misconfigured

LibrePhotos deliberately keeps missing photos in the database instead of immediately deleting them. This is a design decision based on real-world usage patterns: Files often come back - In many cases, the files return when you remount a drive, fix storage configuration, or realize files were moved Preservation of metadata - Your ratings, captions, face tags, and album assignments are preserved Automatic relinking - When files reappear, LibrePhotos can automatically reconnect them to their metadata using hash-based matching
documents.s: Why Does LibrePhotos Keep Missing Photos?

documents.t: LibrePhotos only marks photos as missing during its missing-file check. This check runs automatically as one of the final steps of a photo scan, but only when: the scan is a full scan (a rescan of your whole library), or the scan covers your configured scan directory without targeting a specific list of files. It is therefore skipped for scans that only cover a specific set of files or a single subdirectory — such as an upload, a rescan of some photos or a scan of files a watcher reported — unless that scan is a full scan. It is also skipped when the scan had to skip a folder it could not read. The check looks at your own photos, and for each one whose file can no longer be found on disk, it marks the photo as missing. Simply opening, viewing, or downloading a photo whose file has gone does not mark it as missing — you will just get an error for that one photo. The missing-photo count only updates after a scan has run this check. Common scenarios that cause missing photos: Moving photos to a different folder using a file manager Renaming photo files outside of LibrePhotos External hard drive not mounted at startup Network attached storage (NAS) disconnected Changed mount points in Docker configuration Cloud storage sync issues
documents.s: When Photos Get Marked as Missing

documents.t: New in 1.4.0 If the disk, network share or Docker bind mount that holds your photos is gone but its folder still exists, the scan directory looks empty, and every photo would be marked missing. LibrePhotos refuses to do that. The scan job fails, and nothing is changed, when: the scan directory does not exist or cannot be read, the scan directory is empty while you have photos in it, or the missing-file check finds that more than the Missing photos limit (an admin setting in Site settings, 50% by default) of your photos, and more than 100 photos, would lose all their files. The job's error says how many, for example "4,812 of 5,003 photos would be marked missing. Nothing was changed. Is the library mounted?". Mount the library again and run the scan once more. If you really deleted most of your photos on purpose, ask an administrator to set the Missing photos limit to 100% (which turns the check off), scan, and set it back afterwards.
documents.s: When a Scan Asks "Is the Library Mounted?"

documents.t: LibrePhotos gives you two ways to spot missing photos:

Click your avatar in the top-right corner and select Library. If any of your photos are missing, a red "N Missing Photos" badge appears next to the Photos heading; it is hidden when the count is zero. Hover over the badge to read a short explanation of how LibrePhotos marks photos as missing. Caution Clicking the badge opens the Remove missing photos confirmation dialog, which permanently deletes those photos from the database. Hover only, unless deletion is what you intend.

A missing photo keeps its thumbnail, so it still appears normally in the timeline and albums. The difference only shows in the photo details view: because the file has been detached from the photo, the filename is shown as "Unknown filename" and the folder-path breadcrumb is hidden.
You have several options for dealing with missing photos:

If you know where the files went: Move or copy the files back to their original location If you've moved them to a new location within your scanned directories, LibrePhotos can automatically relink them Run a photo scan to update the database

If the issue is related to mounting or storage: Ensure external drives are properly mounted Check Docker volume mounts in your configuration Verify network storage is accessible Restart LibrePhotos after fixing storage issues Run a scan from the Library page (avatar menu → Library → Scan library → Scan) so LibrePhotos re-checks and relinks the restored files

LibrePhotos automatically relinks photos when files reappear: During regular photo scans, the system uses hash-based matching If a file with the same content hash appears anywhere in your scanned directories, it will be automatically linked to the existing photo metadata This works even if the file has been renamed or moved to a different folder To trigger automatic relinking: Click your avatar in the top-right corner and select Library (or press Ctrl+K and search for "Library") In the Scan library row, click Scan to perform a new scan (a full re-read of every file is available as Rescan in the dropdown next to it) LibrePhotos will detect and relink matching files

If you're certain the files are permanently gone: Open the Library page (avatar menu → Library) Next to the Photos heading, click the red "N Missing Photos" badge — it only appears when your library actually has missing photos The Remove missing photos dialog says how many photos it deletes. Check that number, then click Confirm This will permanently remove all missing photos from the database, including: Photo metadata and EXIF information Thumbnails Face detections Album associations Ratings and captions The same action is also available from the Spotlight command palette (Ctrl+K) as Delete missing photos. Caution Deleting missing photos is permanent. Make sure the files are truly gone and won't be restored before using this option.

Problem: Your external drive containing photos wasn't mounted when LibrePhotos started. Solution: Mount the external drive Restart the LibrePhotos container to pick up the mounted drive The photos should automatically become available again

Problem: You changed your Docker volume configuration and the photo paths no longer match. Solution: Update your Docker configuration to use the original mount point, or Move your photos to match the new mount point Restart LibrePhotos Run a scan from the Library page to update the database

Problem: You reorganized your photo collection using a file manager. Solution: If the new location is within your scanned directories, just run a scan from the Library page (Scan library → Scan) LibrePhotos will detect the files by hash and automatically relink them The original metadata, ratings, and face tags will be preserved
documents.s: Scenario: Files Moved to Different Folder

documents.t: Problem: Photos show as missing after moving them to trash. Solution: If you want to keep them: Restore the files from trash and run a scan If you want to remove them: Use the "N Missing Photos" badge on the Library page (or the Delete missing photos action in the Spotlight palette) to clean up the database

LibrePhotos is working on implementing real-time file system monitoring that will: Automatically detect when files are moved or renamed Immediately update photo paths without manual scans Significantly reduce cases where photos are marked as missing Provide instant relinking when files are moved within scanned directories This real-time monitoring will use file system watchers (inotify on Linux, FSEvents on macOS) to track changes as they happen, making the missing photos feature even more seamless.

Trash Management - Learn about LibrePhotos' trash system Job System - Understanding long-running jobs such as "Delete missing photos", and how to monitor them in the Admin area Auto Scan - Configure automatic photo scanning

UhuruPhotos is a native Android client for LibrePhotos, written using the latest Android technologies. It is the most feature complete app for LibrePhotos. It aims to become a full-featured photo album replacement, including features like offline support, backup and sync etc. Uploads stay "Queued" UhuruPhotos only uploads, even the photos you pick yourself, while Cloud backup & sync is on in its account menu and it has every permission it asks for (full photo access, not selected photos only). Check its network and charging requirements for sync too. With sync on, it also uploads every photo of its feed that is not on the server yet. Uploading must also be allowed on the server (Allow uploads in the admin settings), and your user needs a scan directory. The app is currently in open beta on the Google Play Store. You can contact the author on gitter or discord for information.

LibrePhotos Mobile is the official app: an offline-first app for Android and iOS that keeps a local copy of your library for offline browsing and can back up your camera roll to your server. Not released yet: LibrePhotos Mobile is not on the Google Play Store, the App Store, F-Droid, or TestFlight yet. You can try it by running it from the source code. See the LibrePhotos Mobile guide for how to try it, first login, offline mode, backup, and sync. It is meant to replace the original React Native app. That app's .apk builds on the releases page are no longer updated.

LibrePhotos Mobile is the official app. It stores a local copy of your library on the device, so you can browse your photos, albums, and people with no connection at all — the network is used only to catch the app up with the server and to back up new photos from your phone. It runs on Android and iOS. Not released yet LibrePhotos Mobile has not been published anywhere yet: there is no build on the Google Play Store, the App Store, F-Droid, or TestFlight, and no .apk of it on the GitHub releases page. Until it is, the only way to use it is to run it from the source code, as described below. If you want an app you can install from a store today, see UhuruPhotos.
