The app lives in apps/mobile/ of the LibrePhotos repository. To run it you need a computer with Node.js 24 and a checkout of the repository: git clone https://github.com/LibrePhotos/librephotos.git cd librephotos npm ci # installs the app and the shared API client cd apps/mobile Then pick one of two ways to get it onto your phone: Expo Go (quickest). Install the free Expo Go app on your phone, run npx expo start --go on the computer, and scan the QR code it prints. The phone has to reach the computer over the network, and Expo Go loads the app from it, so keep expo start running while you use the app. This works on Android and on iPhone. Development build (closer to a real install). On Android, with Android Studio and a phone connected over USB (or an emulator), run npx expo run:android. It builds the app and installs it on the device as LibrePhotos. Background backup and the share target behave best in a development build. On iOS a development build needs a Mac with Xcode and a paid Apple Developer account. The developer guide and the app README cover the setup in more detail. Problems and feedback are welcome on the issue tracker with the mobile label.

When you first open the app you are asked for your server address before anything else — this is a self-hosted app, so it needs to know where your LibrePhotos lives. In the Server field, enter the same address you use to reach LibrePhotos in a browser, for example photos.example.com or 192.168.1.10:3000. The protocol is optional. Wait for the connection check to succeed. Sign in with your LibrePhotos username and password. Your login is stored securely on the device. After the first sign-in the app begins downloading a copy of your library in the background (see Offline mode).

After the first sync, the app keeps a local mirror of your library — photos, albums, people, and shared items — together with grid thumbnails. That means you can open the app in airplane mode and still: browse the full timeline and scroll through every photo's thumbnail, open albums, people, places, things, and tags, favorite, hide, trash/restore, rate, caption, and add or remove photos from albums. Changes you make offline are saved immediately and queued. The next time the app is online it sends them to the server automatically. A star rating is written to the photo's file or XMP sidecar when Write edits to files is on, the same as a favorite set on the web. Star ratings New in 1.3.0 Until this fix, a star rating set in the app showed on the phone but never reached the server. Saving ratings needs a build of the app that includes the fix and a server newer than 1.2.1 (1.3.0 or later); an older server rejects the rating and the app shows an error. Ratings set before the fix exist only on that phone, so set them again once both are updated. Full-resolution originals are fetched on demand when you open a photo, so viewing an original still needs a connection unless it is a photo already on your device.

The app can back up new photos and videos from your phone's camera roll to your LibrePhotos server. Open the Backup tab. Grant photo-library access when prompted. On iOS you can grant access to all photos or a limited selection — the app backs up whatever it is allowed to see. Choose which albums to back up (for example only your Camera roll). Set the conditions: back up on Wi-Fi only and/or only while charging. Backup needs two things an admin sets up on the server: Uploads must be enabled. The Allow uploads switch in the admin area has to be on. That switch is the authoritative setting; the ALLOW_UPLOAD environment variable only supplies its initial default (see Environment variables). Your account needs a Scan Directory that exists on the server. Uploaded files are saved in its uploads/web/ folder, or in the web/ folder inside the upload folder an admin set for you (see Upload folder). See How to Change Your Scan Directory. If either is missing, the server rejects the upload. The Backup tab shows progress and a per-item queue. Photos already on the server (matched by content, so duplicates are never re-uploaded) are skipped. A backed- up photo's badge flips from pending to synced once the server confirms it. Backup continues in the background within the limits your phone's operating system allows; keeping the app in the foreground is the fastest way to clear a large backlog. New in 1.5.0 After an upload the server still has to make the photo's thumbnails before it shows up in your timeline. Until the app's next sync brings it in, the Backup tab counts it as processing on the server, its queue row says Processing on server, and its grid tile shows an hourglass instead of the upload arrow. The Backup tab only says everything is backed up once the server has finished.

Open Sync status (from Settings) to see what the app is doing: the last sync time and result, how many items were added, updated, or removed, a running log you can export to attach to a bug report. Because the local copy is disposable, the app can always recover from a bad state by re-syncing from scratch. If counts ever drift from the server the app schedules this automatically, and you can trigger it yourself from the Sync status screen. A re-sync never loses server data — it just rebuilds the local mirror.

The app can remind you about your memories — photos from this day in previous years. Turn on Memories reminder in Settings and pick a time: on each day that has memories you get a local notification at that time saying from how many earlier years they are, and tapping it opens the memories. Days without memories get no notification. The reminders are planned on the device two weeks ahead, from the photos the app has synced, so they work without any push service. They are planned again whenever you open the app, after each sync, and when you change the time or the app language. If the app is not opened or synced for two weeks, the reminders stop until it is.

LibrePhotos Mobile registers as a share target. From another app — Photos, a browser, a messaging app — use the system Share sheet and pick LibrePhotos to send images into your library. On Android this works in a development build (not in Expo Go, which registers as its own app); on iOS the share extension is being finalized.

To enable LibrePhotos to run its machine learning features offline, you can manually download and place the required models by following the steps outlined below. This guide assumes that you have access to the Internet initially to download the models and then configure LibrePhotos to run in an offline environment.

Manually download the necessary models from their respective URLs. Below is a list of models used by LibrePhotos, along with their download links. OpenCLIP is always needed. New in 1.4.0 The captioning and face recognition models are optional; skip the ones whose feature you turned off (see Running with minimal machine learning), and LibrePhotos does not ask for them either. openclip_vitb32 (Tags, semantic search and similar photos; always required) https://huggingface.co/derneuere/librephotos_models/resolve/main/openclip_vitb32/visual.onnx https://huggingface.co/derneuere/librephotos_models/resolve/main/openclip_vitb32/textual.onnx https://huggingface.co/derneuere/librephotos_models/resolve/main/openclip_vitb32/tokenizer.json https://huggingface.co/derneuere/librephotos_models/resolve/main/openclip_vitb32/preprocess.json https://huggingface.co/derneuere/librephotos_models/resolve/main/openclip_vitb32/LICENSE lfm2_vl_450m (Captioning; optional, not needed with FEATURE_IMAGE_CAPTIONING=false or Captioning model None) https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/LFM2.5-VL-450M-ONNX/resolve/main/onnx/vision_encoder_q4.onnx https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/LFM2.5-VL-450M-ONNX/resolve/main/onnx/vision_encoder_q4.onnx_data https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/LFM2.5-VL-450M-ONNX/resolve/main/onnx/embed_tokens_q4.onnx https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/LFM2.5-VL-450M-ONNX/resolve/main/onnx/embed_tokens_q4.onnx_data https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/LFM2.5-VL-450M-ONNX/resolve/main/onnx/decoder_model_merged_q4.onnx https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/LFM2.5-VL-450M-ONNX/resolve/main/onnx/decoder_model_merged_q4.onnx_data Tokenizer: https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/LFM2.5-VL-450M-ONNX/resolve/main/tokenizer.json buffalo_sc (Face recognition — default model; optional, not needed with FEATURE_FACE_DETECTION=false) URL: https://github.com/deepinsight/insightface/releases/download/v0.7/buffalo_sc.zip Only download the model selected in Site settings → Face recognition model. The other options use the same release, e.g. buffalo_s.zip, buffalo_m.zip, buffalo_l.zip, antelopev2.zip.

Once the models are downloaded, place them in the following directory: <LibrePhotos Media Root Directory>/data_models/ MEDIA_ROOT is not something you set directly — it is derived from BASE_DATA (default /), so inside the container it is always /protected_media. On the host it is whichever directory you mounted to /protected_media. With the standard docker-compose install that is ${data}/protected_media, which defaults to ./librephotos/data/protected_media/, so the models go in ./librephotos/data/protected_media/data_models/. openclip_vitb32 files -> Place all five in <MEDIA_ROOT>/data_models/openclip_vitb32/ under their own names lfm2_vl_450m files -> Place all seven in <MEDIA_ROOT>/data_models/lfm2_vl_450m/ under their own names. The .onnx_data files hold the weights the small .onnx graphs point at, so the names must not change. buffalo_sc.zip -> Unpack into <MEDIA_ROOT>/data_models/face_recognition/models/buffalo_sc/ (the folder should contain the .onnx files)
documents.s: Step 2: Place the Models in the Correct Location

documents.t: Ensure that all models are correctly placed and unpacked in their respective directories. The structure should look something like this: data_models/ ├── openclip_vitb32/ │ ├── visual.onnx │ ├── textual.onnx │ ├── tokenizer.json │ ├── preprocess.json │ └── LICENSE ├── lfm2_vl_450m/ │ ├── vision_encoder_q4.onnx │ ├── vision_encoder_q4.onnx_data │ ├── embed_tokens_q4.onnx │ ├── embed_tokens_q4.onnx_data │ ├── decoder_model_merged_q4.onnx │ ├── decoder_model_merged_q4.onnx_data │ └── tokenizer.json └── face_recognition/ └── models/ └── buffalo_sc/

Even with every model stored locally, these settings still reach the Internet by default: Site settings → Map tiles defaults to PhotoPrism (default), which loads the map background from https://cdn.photoprism.app/maps/default.json every time a map is shown. The OpenStreetMap option is not an offline alternative either — it fetches tiles from tile.openstreetmap.org and fonts from fonts.openmaptiles.org. On an offline install, select None (hide map), which turns off map rendering and makes no external requests. Site settings → Map provider (reverse geocoding) is ExifTool (offline, built in) on a new install: it looks place names up in a database that ships with LibrePhotos and needs no Internet access. It names towns, not streets; see Offline place names with ExifTool. An install set up before 1.4.0 keeps the provider it had, usually Nominatim (OpenStreetMap), which calls the public Nominatim service during scans; without Internet access these calls fail and are only logged as a warning, so photos keep their coordinates but get no place names. Select ExifTool there, then Look up place names again under Admin area → Admin tools (see Switching the provider). The place search in the location picker still needs Nominatim, so it does not work offline; clicking the map and pasting coordinates do. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0 there was no offline provider, so place names were unavailable offline. New in 1.5.0 Site settings → Check for new releases asks api.github.com once a day which release is the newest. Offline that request fails, and the switch only says so. To send nothing at all, set UPDATE_CHECK=false (updateCheck=false in .env), which also locks the switch off; see Checking for new releases.
documents.s: Step 4: Turn Off the Online Map Services

documents.t: You can now run LibrePhotos without an active Internet connection for the machine learning features. The application will use the models you manually downloaded and placed in the data_models directory.
LibrePhotos can display your photos on an interactive map based on their GPS coordinates. This page explains how geolocation works and how to get the most out of the Places feature.

When you take a photo with a GPS-enabled device (smartphone, camera with GPS, etc.), the location is stored in the photo's EXIF metadata as latitude and longitude coordinates. LibrePhotos reads these coordinates during the scan process: Composite:GPSLatitude - The latitude coordinate Composite:GPSLongitude - The longitude coordinate The scan stores the position right away, also when reverse geocoding is turned off, so the photo shows up on the map before (or without) a place name. The date rules use it in the same scan: a video's creation time or a photo's GPS time is stored in UTC, and the photo's position tells which time zone to turn it into. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0 the position was only stored by the geocoding job after the scan, so on the first scan these dates fell back to your default time zone; Rescan fixes photos scanned before. GPS edited in another program is picked up by the next scan: a photo you geotag in digiKam, darktable or a GPX tagger gets the new position and, once the geocoding job has run, its new place. When the GPS is removed from the file (for example with exiftool -gps:all= before sharing a folder), the photo loses its position, its place and its Places albums too. A location you set in LibrePhotos (see Setting a Location Manually) is kept either way. Photos indexed before this change keep a position the file no longer has, because LibrePhotos cannot tell whether you set it; new GPS in their files still replaces it. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0 a scan never changed or removed a position once the photo had one.

GPS coordinates alone are just numbers. To show meaningful place names (like "Paris, France" or "Central Park, New York"), LibrePhotos uses reverse geocoding - a process that converts coordinates into human-readable addresses. You can configure your preferred geocoding provider in Admin area → Site settings: Provider API Key Required Notes ExifTool (offline, built in) No Default for new installs. Works offline; names the nearest town, not streets (see Offline place names) Nominatim (OpenStreetMap) No Free and open source; names streets; about one lookup per second Mapbox Yes Commercial service with free tier MapTiler Yes Commercial service with free tier OpenCage Yes Commercial service with free tier TomTom Yes Commercial service with free tier Recommended Setup ExifTool is the recommended option: it is built in, needs no API key and no Internet access, and your photos' coordinates never leave your server. It names towns rather than streets. New in 1.4.0 New installs start with it; an install that has already looked up place names keeps the provider it had (Nominatim, unless you chose another), see Switching the provider. Choose Nominatim if you want street and point-of-interest names. It is free and needs no API key, but it receives the coordinates of your photos. To respect Nominatim's public terms of use, LibrePhotos limits itself to about one lookup per second for this provider, and that limit is shared across all background workers — adding more workers won't speed it up. The first scan of a large geotagged library will therefore take a while, and places keep filling in after the scan reports done. If you have tens of thousands of geotagged photos, a commercial provider with an API key geocodes far faster. Offline place names with ExifTool​ New in 1.4.0 Choose ExifTool (offline, built in) as the Map provider to look place names up on your own server. ExifTool, which LibrePhotos already uses to read metadata, comes with a database of the world's towns, so the lookup needs no Internet connection and no API key, has no rate limit (about 9 ms per photo instead of more than a second with Nominatim), and your photos' coordinates never leave the server. What to expect: Town level. A photo gets its nearest town or neighbourhood (towns of 2,000 people or more), the district, the region and the country, for example Zermatt, Visp District, Valais, Switzerland. There are no street, park or point-of-interest names; choose Nominatim or a commercial provider if you want those. A name that repeats on several levels is kept once, so Lisbon is Lisbon, Portugal. Names in English or Latin script. The names come from GeoNames and are the same for every user (Germany, Tokyo), not in the language of each country. Nothing within 50 km means no place. A photo farther than 50 km from any town (open sea, a large national park, the Antarctic) keeps its position and stays on the map, but gets no place name and joins no Places album, rather than the name of a town far away. Borders. The database knows towns, not borders: a photo taken close to a border can get the name of a town across it (on Kilimanjaro, the nearest town is in Kenya). Place search in the location picker still uses Nominatim, because ExifTool cannot search addresses. Only the text you type is sent, never a photo's position. On a server without Internet access the search fails, but clicking the map and pasting coordinates still work. Place names from ExifTool come from GeoNames and are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Switching the provider​ Switching the Map provider does not rename photos that already have a place: new photos, and photos whose position changes, get names from the new provider, so your Places albums mix the names of both. New in 1.4.0 To give every photo the names of the new provider, an admin opens Admin area → Admin tools and clicks Start next to Look up place names again, then confirms. A Look up place names job asks the provider set now for the place of every photo with a location, for every user, and you can follow it in Worker logs: Each photo moves to the Places albums of its new names. Places albums under the old names end up empty, favourited or shared ones included. The day albums (and the memories built from them) name their places again as the job reaches their photos. Event titles keep their wording until the event albums are generated again (Regenerate event titles). With ExifTool it takes minutes for a large library. With an online provider it takes about a second per photo (Nominatim's limit), so hours for tens of thousands of photos. A photo whose lookup fails keeps its old place, and the next run tries it again. Place names in your language​ New in 1.5.0 Online providers name places in their own default language: English for some, the local name for Nominatim (Wien for Vienna, Москва for Moscow). To ask for another language, an admin picks it under Admin area → Site settings → Place name language, right below the Map provider. Provider default, the default, asks for no language, as before. Nominatim, OpenCage, TomTom and MapTiler answer in the language you pick. Nominatim also takes a list in order of preference: type de,en into the field for German names, or English where a place has no German one. Mapbox and the offline ExifTool provider always answer in their own language; the field is disabled while one of them is the Map provider, and it keeps your choice for when you switch. The language applies to new lookups. Photos named already keep their names until you look them up again: after a change, the setting offers Look up place names again, the same job as in Admin tools (see Switching the provider). It is one language for the whole server. The GEOCODE_LANGUAGE environment variable sets it on the first set-up. Which name a photo is filed under​ Every provider answers several names, from the street or town up to the country. The day albums, memories, event titles and the map button of an event ("Zermatt on map") use the town (Zermatt, not the canton Valais); the place tree uses the country, the region and the town; the location timeline uses the country. New in 1.4.0 These read the level each name has. Up to 1.3.0 they took the name at a fixed position in the list, which named the region for some providers, and the place tree left out places with fewer than three names (Lisbon, Portugal). Photos geocoded before 1.4.0 keep the names they showed until you look the place names up again.

LibrePhotos renders maps with MapLibre GL. By default the map background (the "tiles") comes from PhotoPrism's free tile server, which provides: Smooth, high-quality vector maps Fast rendering and zooming No API key required for map display Works offline once tiles are cached Admins can change where tiles come from under Admin area → Site settings → Map tiles, which sits directly below the Map provider select. Three options are available: PhotoPrism (default): MapLibre vector tiles from cdn.photoprism.app and maps.photoprism.app. OpenStreetMap: raster tiles from tile.openstreetmap.org (label glyphs from fonts.openmaptiles.org). None (hide map): no map is rendered anywhere; a placeholder is shown instead. In dark mode every map is shown darkened: LibrePhotos inverts the light map in the browser and turns its colours back, so water stays blue and parks stay green, and the place markers keep their colours. This works for both tile sources and loads nothing extra. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, maps stayed light in dark mode. This setting is global. Choosing None hides the map in every map view, including the Places page, album location maps, the photo-info mini-map, and the location picker. The initial value comes from the MAP_TILE_PROVIDER environment variable (default photoprism), but it is an admin-editable site setting thereafter, so you don't need to restart to change it.

The Places page (/album/places) shows your photos on an interactive map, each where it was taken, and under the map the places (Places albums) that have a photo in the part of the world the map shows. New in 1.5.0 The map shows photos, not place names: Photos where they were taken: every photo with a position is a point at that position. Photos taken within about a metre of each other are one point, with their number on it. Clusters count photos: when zoomed out, nearby points are grouped into a cluster, and the number on it is how many photos it holds. A photo counts once, whatever number of place names it has. Click to zoom: click a cluster to zoom in until it splits. Click to open: click a point, or a cluster once you are zoomed in to street level, to see how many photos were taken there and the newest few. Click a thumbnail, or Open N photos, to step through them in the photo viewer. Places in view: as you pan and zoom, the grid below lists the places with at least one photo inside the map. A country or a region stays in the list while one of its photos is in view. The line under the title says how many photos are on the map and how many places are in view. A taller map: drag the grip under the map down to make it taller (up to 560 pixels), or focus it and use the arrow keys. The page remembers the height. Up to 1.4.0 the map drew one marker per place name at the centre of that place: a photo showed up once for its street, once for its town and once for its region, a cluster counted place names rather than photos, and markers sat at the centre of a county where no photo was taken. The map and its counts only ever show your own photos. Hidden photos and photos in the trash are left out, and photos other users shared with you are not on it.
New in 1.5.0 Name the places that matter to you, such as Home, Office or Grandma's, and LibrePhotos files every photo taken there under that name, whatever the map provider calls the street.

Open Albums → Places and click Add place above the map. The map grows so there is room to draw. Click the map where the place is. A circle appears around that spot; the map zooms in if it is too small to see. Click elsewhere to move it. Drag the white dot on the circle's edge, or the Radius slider, to make it the size of the place: from 25 m (a house) to 2 km (a village). Type a Name, pick an icon, and leave Use the name in event titles on to have events taken there called "Sunday at Home" rather than "Sunday in Munich". While you draw, the editor says how many of your photos were taken inside the circle and shows the newest few. When the circle overlaps another of your places, it says how many photos are inside both. Click Save place. The photos taken inside are filed under the place at once. Your places are drawn on the map as blue circles with their names, and listed under Your places above the places in view, whatever part of the map you look at. Click one to open its page with its photos by day and its circle on a small map; Edit place there opens the editor on the Places map again, and ⋮ → Delete place deletes it. Deleting a place keeps its photos and their place names from the map provider.

A photo is in a place when its position lies inside the circle. A photo inside two of your places is in the smaller one: a photo of the garden is in Home, not in the neighbourhood around it. Photos join and leave on their own: when a scan finds a new or changed position in a file, and when you set or remove a location by hand (for one photo or many). Moving or resizing a place files your photos again. A photo without a position is in no place. Give it a location first (see Setting a Location Manually). A photo in one of your places shows the place's name first in the photo's details, with the map provider's name under it, and searching for the place's name finds it. An event mostly taken in one of your places (at least half of its photos) is called after it, such as "Sunday at Home" or "Saturday with Anna at Home", once its title is generated: new events right away, existing ones after Regenerate event titles. Turn Use the name in event titles off to keep the town in the title. The web app shows these titles; the mobile app still shows the town. You can have up to 100 places.
documents.s: Which photos are in a place

documents.t: A place called Home tells where you live, so your places are private. Their names and circles are never shown to anyone else: not in albums or events you share, not in photos shared with other users (their Shared with you page groups them by the map provider's place names only), not on public links, and not in another user's search. The titles of shared events keep the town. Your places are not written to your photo files either.

Go to Admin area → Site settings Select your preferred Map provider — this is the geocoding service used to turn coordinates into place names If using a commercial provider, enter your key in the API key for map provider field Optionally, choose the Map tiles source directly below (PhotoPrism, OpenStreetMap, or None) — this controls the map background rather than geocoding Save the settings

Click your avatar (top right) and choose Library In the Scan library card, click Scan to pick up newly added photos. If your photos are already indexed, open the dropdown next to the button and choose Rescan instead — a plain scan skips files that haven't changed The scan extracts GPS coordinates and performs reverse geocoding See Library Management for the full list of Library page actions.
Navigate to Albums → Places to see your photos on the map.

Once your photos have location data: Search by location: Search for photos by place name (e.g., "Paris", "beach") Events with places: Event titles include the location Location timeline: See where you've been over time Place tree: Hierarchical view of all your locations Photo info: Individual photos show their location on a mini-map (when map display is enabled), and you can set or correct a photo's location from there

If a photo has no GPS data, or has the wrong location, you can set it by hand: Open the photo and find the location line in the info sidebar. Click the pencil (Update location) next to it to open the Pick location dialog. Set the position by searching for a place name, pasting coordinates such as 48.8566, 2.3522 into the search box and choosing Use coordinates, clicking or dragging the marker on the map, or clicking the crosshair button to use your browser's current location. Check the place name under the map: it is the name the photo gets when you save. It reads Place name unavailable when the server has no name for the spot (the coordinates are saved anyway), and says so when place names are turned off on the server. Click Save. The photo is reverse-geocoded immediately and added to the matching place albums — no rescan required. The pencil is not shown on publicly shared photos. If maps are turned off in Site settings, the map pane is hidden but place-name search, pasted coordinates and "use my current location" still work. New in 1.5.0 Up to 1.4.0, the place-name search found nothing when the Map provider was OpenCage, Mapbox or MapTiler. A photo without a location opens the dialog where the nearest geotagged photo taken within a day of it was taken, or on a world map when there is none. The browser only asks for your position when you click the crosshair button. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0 it asked as soon as the dialog opened, and started over Paris without permission. New in 1.4.0 Above the search box, Copy from a photo taken nearby in time shows up to 20 of your photos that have a location and were taken within a day of this one, nearest first, each with its place and how long before or after it was taken. Click one to put the marker on its location; its place name is shown at once. Handy for camera photos taken next to a phone that recorded GPS.

New in 1.4.0 Photos from a camera without GPS, scans and screenshots often need the same location. Select them on the timeline or any photo page (or use Select all), open the ⋮ photo actions menu and choose Edit info → Set location…: The dialog says how many of the selected photos already have a location. By default only the photos without a location get the new one; choose All N photos to replace the others too. The dialog then names the places that would be replaced. When every selected photo has a location, saving replaces them all, and the dialog says so. Pick the spot as for a single photo: search, paste coordinates, click the map, use your current location, or click a photo under Copy from a photo taken nearby in time (your geotagged photos taken within a day of the selection). Click Set location for N photos. The place name is looked up once for all of them. Each photo gets the position, its place albums and location search, and its own entry in the edit history; the confirmation says how many photos got the location and how many kept their own. If the place name cannot be looked up, the coordinates are saved anyway and the confirmation says so. With Write edits to files on, the new location is written to the photo files or sidecars in one background job. To remove the location of photos, use Remove location on each photo.
documents.s: Setting the location of many photos

documents.t: New in 1.4.0 If a photo has a wrong location (a phone that reused a stale GPS fix, a scan that inherited the scanner's position), open the Pick location dialog and click Remove location, then confirm. The photo leaves the map, its place albums and location search, and a rescan does not bring the location back; set a location again in the same dialog. With Write edits to files set to Save to media file, the location is also removed from the photo file; with Save to sidecar, it is removed from the sidecar, and a location stored in the photo file itself stays there. With Off the photo file is not changed. The dialog says which applies. Remove location is only shown for a photo that has one. If no place name can be found for the new position (reverse geocoding is turned off, the provider fails or rate limits, or the spot has no address, such as open sea), the new coordinates are still saved. The photo then drops the place it had before: it leaves its old place albums, is no longer found by searching the old place name, and the info sidebar shows the coordinates instead of a place name. When the lookup failed, a notice says that the place name could not be looked up; when it worked but there is no place at that spot, the confirmation says so instead. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, the photo kept the old place name and albums in that case, and the dialog reported a plain success.

Check if photos have GPS data: Open a photo's info panel and look for GPS coordinates Scan for new photos: If you recently added photos, run a Scan from the Library page Check geocoding provider: Ensure your geocoding provider is configured correctly in Admin area → Site settings. A commercial provider with a missing or invalid API key fails silently — the scan reports success but no place names are stored Scan again after fixing the provider: Go to Library → Scan library and click Scan. The geocoding job after it looks up every photo whose position has no place name yet, including the ones whose lookup failed before, but not the ones where the provider found no place, such as open sea. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0 it only looked up photos added since the previous geolocation run, so a full Rescan was needed Give geocoding time to finish: Geocoding runs as a background job after the scan. With Nominatim on a large library this can take a while, and places keep filling in after the scan reports done — wait before re-scanning

Not all devices embed GPS data in photos Indoor photos may not have accurate GPS Some cameras require GPS to be explicitly enabled Check if location services were enabled when the photo was taken A rescan cannot add coordinates that were never in the file. To place such a photo yourself, see Setting a Location Manually.

Check your internet connection Check Admin area → Site settings → Map tiles. If it is set to None, maps are disabled on purpose With PhotoPrism (default), the tiles come from cdn.photoprism.app and maps.photoprism.app With OpenStreetMap, they come from tile.openstreetmap.org and fonts.openmaptiles.org instead Ensure the relevant domains aren't blocked by your firewall or ad blocker. If the PhotoPrism domains are unreachable, switching Map tiles to OpenStreetMap (or None to hide the map) is an alternative

GPS coordinates in photos can reveal sensitive location information When sharing photos, consider stripping EXIF data if privacy is a concern LibrePhotos keeps your location data private within your instance Opening a map fetches tiles for the area around your photos, which reveals their approximate location to the selected tile provider. The photo-info mini-map zooms in tightly, so the tiles it requests pinpoint that photo's location fairly precisely You control this with Map tiles in Admin area → Site settings: PhotoPrism (default, tiles from cdn.photoprism.app / maps.photoprism.app), OpenStreetMap (tiles from tile.openstreetmap.org, which shifts the exposure to a different provider rather than removing it), or None to disable map display entirely so no third-party tile requests are made

New in 1.5.0 Every photo has rights: a copyright notice, a creator and a license. They say who made the photo and what others may do with it. LibrePhotos reads them from your files, lets you set them for one photo or many, and can give new photos your own default.

A license is one of this fixed list. Each Creative Commons license links to its official deed on creativecommons.org, which explains it in full. License What others may do All rights reserved Look at the photo, but not reuse it without your permission. CC BY 4.0 Share and adapt it, also commercially, if they credit you. CC BY-SA 4.0 Share and adapt it, also commercially, if they credit you and share their adaptation under the same license. CC BY-NC 4.0 Share and adapt it for non-commercial use, if they credit you. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 Share and adapt it for non-commercial use, if they credit you and share their adaptation under the same license. CC BY-ND 4.0 Share it unchanged, also commercially, if they credit you. CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 Share it unchanged for non-commercial use, if they credit you. CC0 1.0 Anything, without asking or crediting: you give up your rights. Public domain (Public Domain Mark 1.0) Anything: the photo is free of known copyright, for example because it is very old. There is no free-text license and no field for your own license link: a link to a license always goes to the deed above.

Open a photo and the info panel (i) has a Rights section below the tags; the photo page has a Rights card. It shows the license with its marks and a link to its deed (What … allows), the copyright notice and the creator. A value marked From file is the one the photo's file states; the others were set in LibrePhotos. Click the pencil to edit them: Copyright (for example © 2026 Anna Berger), Creator and License, then the check mark to save. Leaving a field empty removes it. Each change is recorded in the photo's edit history and, with Write edits to files on, written to the file or its sidecar. A photo without any rights says so. If you set default rights, the section offers Use my default, which fills in the photo's empty fields from it.

Select photos, open Photo actions (the ⋮ in the selection bar) and pick Edit info → Set rights…. The dialog shows the license, creator and copyright the selected photos share. Where they differ, the field says Mixed: keep each photo's. Only the fields you change are set; the others stay as each photo has them, and a field you empty is removed from every photo. {year} in the copyright becomes the year each photo was taken, so © {year} Anna Berger gives a photo from 2019 © 2019 Anna Berger (a photo without a date gets the year it was added). Values a photo's file states are kept, so a photo that came with someone else's copyright keeps it. When some of the selected photos have rights from their files, the dialog offers Also change N photos whose rights come from their files to replace those too.

Settings > Metadata > Rights for your photos holds a creator, a copyright notice (with {year}) and a license, saved with your other settings. New photos get them when they are scanned, for each field their file does not state. This is recorded as your edit, but a scan never writes to your files: use Write existing edits to files to put them there. Photos you already have keep their rights until you click Apply to my photos…. The dialog says how many photos it reaches and asks whether to Only fill in what is missing (a copyright, creator or license a photo already has stays) or change Every photo. Changing the default later does not change photos that already have it, so a published photo is never relicensed behind your back.

A license is your deliberate statement of what others may do with a photo, so a public album, a public photo and a photo link show the rights of a photo that has a license, whatever the sharing switches say: the license, and with it the copyright notice and the creator. A photo without a license shows visitors no rights at all, not even a copyright or creator its file carries: cameras and apps often write your full name there, and you never chose to publish it. The license can be one you set, your default rights or one the file states. People you share your library with see a photo's rights as you do, with or without a license. Visitors see a License section first in the photo's details (under the photo on a photo link): the license with its marks, the copyright notice and the creator; one sentence on what they may do, and a row each for sharing, changing and commercial use, with what the license asks of them (credit, the same license for adaptations); a link to the license's deed; for a license that asks for credit, How to credit: a line naming the creator, the page and the license with its deed, with a copy button (on plain HTTP, where browsers do not allow copying, the line can be selected). A photo without a license shows visitors no License section.

LibrePhotos reads the rights from these tags, the first one a photo has: Field Tags, best first Copyright XMP:Rights, IPTC:CopyrightNotice, EXIF:Copyright Creator XMP:Creator, IPTC:By-line, EXIF:Artist License XMP-cc:License, then XMP-xmpRights:WebStatement when it is a Creative Commons deed; XMP-xmpRights:Marked set to true without either is All rights reserved (Lightroom's "Copyrighted") A WebStatement that links to anything else, such as your own rights page, is not a license and is left alone. With Write edits to files on, a change is written back: Field Save to sidecar Save to media file Copyright XMP-dc:Rights XMP-dc:Rights and EXIF:Copyright, and IPTC:CopyrightNotice if the file already has IPTC data Creator XMP-dc:Creator XMP-dc:Creator and EXIF:Artist, and IPTC:By-line if the file already has IPTC data License XMP-cc:License and XMP-xmpRights:WebStatement (the deed), XMP-xmpRights:UsageTerms (the license's name and deed), XMP-xmpRights:Marked (true, false for CC0 and the Public Domain Mark) the same Lightroom, digiKam and other apps read these tags, so the license travels with the photo. A copyright or creator is written on one line: line breaks become spaces. A rescan keeps the rights you set in LibrePhotos, like your other edits, and Restore from file takes them from the file again (see How a rescan treats your edits).
LibrePhotos offers several ways to search through your photo library, from quick keyboard-driven navigation to AI-powered semantic search.
The spotlight is a powerful command palette that gives you instant access to search, navigation, and actions — all from the keyboard.

Press any of these keyboard shortcuts to open the spotlight: Shortcut Platform Ctrl + K Windows / Linux Cmd + K macOS Ctrl + P Windows / Linux Cmd + P macOS / Any platform Note Ctrl + P / Cmd + P opens the spotlight rather than the browser's print dialog. Use the browser menu if you need to print the page. You can also click the search field at the top of the page (Search photos, people and places; on a phone it just says Search).

The spotlight provides three types of actions: Search​ Start typing to search across your entire library: People — Search by person name Places — Search by location name Things — Search by detected objects or scene types User albums — Search your album names Free text — Search photo captions and metadata Select "Search for [your query]" to perform a full search and see all matching results. Navigation​ Quickly jump to any page in LibrePhotos: Photos, Albums, My albums, People, Places, Things, Tags, Events, Folders Memories, Favorites, Hidden, Archive, Videos, Screenshots, Documents, Trash, Recently added, Photos without timestamps, Photos without location, photos not in an album New in 1.4.0 Filter photos: the search page with filters and no words Sharing, Review faces (the face dashboard), Statistics, and its sub-pages Place tree, Word clouds, Timeline, Social graph and Face clusters Settings, Profile, Library, Admin area Settings and Profile also expose keyword shortcuts: typing something like password, language, clustering, metadata or llm surfaces entries such as Change password, Change language, Face recognition settings, Metadata settings and Caption context settings, each of which opens the matching Settings or Profile page. Actions​ Trigger common actions directly from the spotlight: Scan photos / Rescan all photos — Start a photo scan Train face recognition / Detect faces in photos — Run face recognition Generate event albums — Group photos into events Remove missing photos — Clean up missing files Toggle dark mode — Switch between light and dark mode

When you perform a search (either from the spotlight or the search bar), LibrePhotos searches across multiple fields: Photo captions (AI-generated and manual) People's names Location names (from reverse geocoding) Keywords and tags embedded in the photo (XMP Subject and IPTC Keywords, including from .xmp sidecar files) — for example, tags applied in Lightroom or digiKam File paths Camera and lens information File type Text recognised in the photo, when text recognition is on and has read the photo (receipts, signs, screenshots) Date fragments in ISO form (e.g. 2024, 2024-01, 2024-01-15) — the timestamp is matched as plain text, so month or weekday names such as "January" or "Thursday" do not match Every word in your query must match, though not necessarily in the same field: searching beach sunset returns only photos where both beach and sunset appear somewhere in the indexed text (caption, person name, location, file path, camera, and so on). Commas separate words the same way spaces do. To search for an exact phrase, wrap it in quotes — "golden gate bridge" matches only photos containing that whole phrase. Accents and letter case do not matter, in either direction: Zurich finds photos taken in Zürich, café finds a caption that says "cafe", and Lodz finds "Łódź". This covers everything in the list above except the date, plus your tags. Text found in photos by OCR is still matched as written. The spotlight's suggestions ignore accents the same way. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, a search had to spell every accent. The upgrade prepares existing photos once, while the database migrates. The search results header also has a media button in the top right for narrowing the results to photos, videos, screenshots or documents, and a Filters button for everything else (see Search Filters). Results are displayed grouped by date, similar to the main timeline view.

Note New in 1.4.0 The filters come to the web app and to the API in the same release. Besides the words you type, a search can be narrowed by the people in the photo, the camera, the exposure, the rating, the day, the location and the file. On the search results page, click Filters next to the media button (on a phone, the filter icon) to open the panel: People: pick one or more people. With several, you get the photos with all of them together. While you type a name, the matching people are listed with the most faces first. New in 1.5.0 Up to 1.4.0, matches stayed in name order. Camera: the maker, the camera and the lens. The lists show the cameras of your own photos, most used first, with how many photos of your library each one took. Exposure: ISO, aperture, focal length and 35 mm equivalent focal length, each as a lowest and a highest value (either can stay empty). A value applies when you leave the field or press Enter. Shortcuts set common ISO and focal length bands in one click. Rating: with star ratings, the fewest stars a photo needs. With the favorite toggle (see the rating style in Settings), one Favorites only switch. Taken: on or after and on or before a day, or This year, Last year and Last 12 months. Location: only photos with GPS coordinates, or only those without. File: Has a RAW file (also finds RAW files paired with a JPEG) and the main file's extension, for example cr3. Photos or videos only stays on the media button. Every change applies at once. The active filters show as chips under the title: the cross on a chip removes that filter, and Clear all removes every filter but keeps your words and the media type. The filters are part of the page address, so you can bookmark or share a filtered search, and Back undoes the last change. To filter without any words, open the spotlight and choose Filter photos, or go to /search/. If a filter cannot be applied, for example a person deleted in the meantime, the page says so and offers to clear the filters. Selecting all results and then acting on them (favorite, hide, tag, share, add to an album, download, move to the trash) acts on exactly the photos the search listed.

The filters are query parameters of GET /api/photos/searchlist/. They combine with each other, with the search words and with the media filter (every condition must hold), and they also work without any search words: /api/photos/searchlist/?camera=X-T5&iso_min=3200 lists every photo taken with that camera at ISO 3200 or more. Parameter Finds photos… camera taken with this camera model, for example X-T5 (the whole name, any letter case) make taken with a camera from this maker, for example FUJIFILM lens taken with this lens model iso_min, iso_max with an ISO speed in this range aperture_min, aperture_max with an f-number in this range, for example aperture_min=1.4&aperture_max=2 focal_min, focal_max with a focal length in this range, in millimetres focal35_min, focal35_max with a 35 mm equivalent focal length in this range rating_min rated at least this many stars (1 to 5) taken_after, taken_before taken on or after, or on or before, this day (2024-03-01) has_location with GPS coordinates (true) or without them (false, the same photos as the No Location page) file_type whose main file is an image or a video, or that have a RAW file (raw, the photos with the RAW badge) extension whose main file has this extension, for example cr3 or .heic person showing this person. Repeat it for several people (person=3&person=7) to find the photos with all of them together Ranges include both ends, and either end can be left out. A photo without the value, for example one whose camera did not record the lens, never matches a filter on it. A value the server cannot read, a range whose lowest value is above its highest, an unknown file extension or someone else's person answers with an error that names the parameter, rather than with an empty result. The camera maker comes from the photo's EXIF data since the release after 1.3.0. Photos scanned before that have none until you rescan them, so make does not find them yet. GET /api/search/metadata-values/?field=camera lists the camera models of your photos with how many photos each one took, most used first. field=make lists the makers and field=lens the lenses. Pick a filter value from there to be sure it matches. The bulk actions take the same parameters in their select-all query. Send show_all_stack_photos: true with them, because search lists every photo of a stack, not only the one the timeline shows. The search words themselves are not part of a select-all, so after a search with words the web app sends the listed photos instead.

Semantic search uses AI (CLIP embeddings) to find photos by meaning rather than exact text matching. It understands the concept behind your query, and those matches are added to the normal text-search results rather than replacing them — so a search returns both the photos whose captions or metadata contain your words and the photos that simply look like what you described. Because of this, a result may not contain every word of your query. For example, searching "sunset at the beach" will find photos that look like a sunset at a beach, even if none of those words appear in the photo's metadata or caption.

Semantic search is disabled by default. It works from CLIP embeddings, which LibrePhotos computes for your photos during a scan, plus a similarity index built from those embeddings. Go to Settings Find the Semantic search max results setting Set it to Top 100, Top 50, or Top 10 — the maximum number of semantically similar photos to add to your results. Matches that fall below an internal similarity threshold are dropped, so you may get fewer than this, and because keyword matches are still included the total number of results can be higher. Turning the setting on also queues a background job that computes CLIP embeddings for any photos that do not have one yet and then builds the similarity index. Semantic results only start appearing once that job has finished, which can take a while on a large library that has never been embedded. The image-similarity service keeps the index on disk under protected_media/similarity/, so it survives a restart of that service, and it is rebuilt automatically each time the backend container starts. The first query after a while without searches can take a moment while the CLIP model loads again, after which queries are fast. Tip You need to have the CLIP embedding calculation job completed for semantic search to work. This runs automatically during photo scanning, or you can trigger it manually from the Library page.

One model turns photos and queries into embeddings and detects the things in your photos: OpenCLIP ViT-B/32, trained by LAION on DataComp-XL and released under the MIT licence. Detecting a photo's things yields its search embedding from the same run, so a scan runs one vision model per photo. There is nothing to choose in the settings. Upgrading to 1.3.0 Releases up to 1.2.x searched with CLIP ViT-B/32 and detected things with another model. After the upgrade a Calculate CLIP embeddings job re-embeds every photo with OpenCLIP in the background and gives it new things from the same run; nothing is deleted first. While it runs, semantic search and similar photos cover the photos converted so far (the index catches up after the first 2,000 photos and then each time the number converted has doubled, so a large library is not held up rebuilding it; up to 1.4.0 it caught up every 2,000 photos), and the Things albums fill up again as photos are processed again. It happens once.

During scanning, LibrePhotos computes a CLIP embedding for each photo — a numerical representation of the image's visual content When you search, your text query is also converted to a CLIP embedding Photos whose embeddings are closest to your query embedding are returned as results Matching photos are returned as a single flat list instead of being grouped by date. The list is not sorted by similarity score — the CLIP ranking only decides which photos come back (the top N you configured), not the order they appear in

When viewing a photo in the lightbox, the Similar photos section in the sidebar shows visually similar photos from your library. These are found using the same CLIP embedding technology as semantic search. Click on any similar photo to navigate directly to it. This is useful for: Finding photos from the same scene or event Discovering visually related content Spotting potential duplicates
There are three kinds of settings at the moment.

Open your profile settings with Account menu > Profile (on a phone, tap your picture at the right end of the bottom bar, then Profile). Here you can change your name, photo, e-mail address, password and language. You can also set whether you want your profile to be accessible globally or not. Avatar, First name, Last name will be shown if you share pictures with other users or when your profile is publically accessible Email is the address your password-reset link is sent to. The Forgot your password? link only appears on the login page once an administrator has configured outgoing e-mail (Admin area → Site settings → Email (SMTP)), and resetting your own password only works if your account has an e-mail address set. If it does not, an administrator can still reset your password for you under Admin area → Users. Change password is for changing your password Language will change the settings Public sharing will set if you can be found globally
These settings are user specific and will affect how scanning and saving works. At the bottom, you can also find experimental settings.

New in 1.4.0 Both the Settings page and the Admin area have an On this page list. On a wide screen it sits to the right of the cards; on a phone or a narrow window it is a row of buttons under the top bar that scrolls sideways. The entry of the card you are looking at is highlighted, and picking one scrolls to its card. Every card also has its own link. Hover over a card's title and click the # next to it to copy the link, for example https://photos.example.com/settings#settings-faces or /admin#admin-services. Opening such a link scrolls straight to that card and outlines it for a moment, which is handy when you point someone to a setting.
This setting affect how much certainty is needed for a tag to be added to a picture. Default Standard

If you set this to Top 100,Top 50, Top 10 you will get semantic search results instead of just looking at the EXIF data. It is disabled as default, because the first search takes a minute to get a response. After that it is fast. Default Disabled. For more information, see Search.

Write edits to files copies some of your edits into your files, so other apps see them. Each option says what it writes. Default Off. Off: edits stay in LibrePhotos. Your files are never changed. Save to sidecar: ratings, dates, rotations, captions, tags, locations and rights are written to an .xmp file next to the photo (an existing one, else a new IMG.jpg.xmp, see Which sidecar is written). The photo itself is not changed. Save to media file: ratings, dates, rotations, captions, tags, locations and rights are written into the photo file itself. This changes your originals, so keep a backup. Rotations are only written into JPEG, PNG, TIFF and WebP files; other formats, such as HEIC, AVIF and RAW, keep their rotation in LibrePhotos. Tags are written as the file's keywords. New in 1.5.0 Copyright notices, creators and licenses are written too (Copyright and licenses); titles are not. Face names are written only with Write face tags to image files (see Face options). The tags each edit writes are listed in EXIF Data, and Undoing write-back says how to take them back. While you edit a date, caption, tags or location in the photo details sidebar, a line under the editor says whether that edit reaches the file. Photos imported from Nextcloud are never written to: LibrePhotos works on a local copy, which the next scan replaces when the file changes on the server, and nothing is uploaded back. Their edits stay in LibrePhotos. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, this setting was called Synchronize metadata to disk, it wrote no captions, tags or locations, and it did write into the local copies of Nextcloud photos. New in 1.4.0 Write existing edits to files, under the choice above, writes the edits you made before turning it on, which are only in LibrePhotos, with Write now. It writes what your photos carry: ratings above 0, dates and locations you set by hand, rotations, captions you wrote, tags (as keywords) and, with Write face tags to image files on, face tags. A photo without any of these gets no write and no new sidecar. The sentence above the button names the kinds and the number of photos; the dialog before it starts lists each kind with its count. Into sidecars it is a plain confirm; into media files it asks in red, because your originals change. It runs as a Write metadata to files job: the row shows how far it got, and the job list has the photos that could not be written. The button waits while Write edits to files is Off or has a change you have not saved. See Writing the edits of a whole library. New in 1.5.0 It also writes the copyright, creator and license you set in LibrePhotos. New in 1.4.0 Rating style picks how you rate photos on the web. Default Favorites. Favorites: one star toggle. Adding a favorite sets the photo's rating to the minimum rating below; removing a favorite sets the rating to 0. That also clears a star rating the photo had, for example a 5-star rating from Lightroom or digiKam, and with Write edits to files on, the 0 is written to the file too. Stars: rate photos with 1 to 5 stars in the photo viewer (keys 0 to 5) and on the photo page, see their stars on the grid, and set them for a selection with Set rating. The favorite toggle is gone in this mode, so a rating only changes when you set it. See Rating photos with stars. Minimum image rating to interpret as favorite will change how favorites are read and saved. EXIF only supports the rating field and does not have a favorite field. In Stars mode it still decides which photos the Favorites page and the timeline's favorites filter show. Default 4 Default timezone is used by the date rules that say "in user default timezone" (for example video creation times, which cameras store in UTC, and file times), and to decide which day Memories counts as today. It does not change how dates are displayed, and LibrePhotos never writes it to your files. Changing it does not re-date photos already in your library: run Rescan, or New in 1.4.0 click Apply under Dates on the Library page afterwards (Applying the rules). Default UTC New in 1.5.0 Rights for your photos, a card of its own under the metadata options, holds the creator, copyright notice ({year} becomes the year a photo was taken) and license your photos get when their files state none: new photos when they are scanned, the photos you already have when you click Apply to my photos…, which asks whether to fill in only what is missing or change every photo. See Copyright and licenses.
Here you can set how timestamps are parsed. You can find more information here

Below the date and time rules is a Burst detection rules editor. It defines the ordered list of rules used when stack detection looks for burst sequences — photos taken in rapid succession. Rules fall into two categories, shown as a Hard or Soft badge: Hard rules are deterministic and enabled by default: EXIF Burst Mode Tag, EXIF Sequence Number and Filename Burst Pattern (for names such as IMG_001_BURST001 or photo (1)). Soft rules are estimates and are present but disabled by default: Timestamp Proximity (photos within about two seconds from the same camera) and Visual Similarity (visually similar consecutive photos). For each rule you can toggle it on or off, delete it, or drag it to reorder the list. Add rule opens a searchable catalogue of further rules — including Filename Burst Suffix Only, Custom Filename Pattern and a looser Timestamp Proximity (Loose) (about five seconds, any camera). Reset to defaults restores the default set. Each rule's parameters are fixed and shown for reference only; there is no parameter editor here.

Always transcode videos converts every video to H.264 as you play it, including the ones your browser could have played as they are. You rarely need it: a video your browser cannot play is converted anyway, without this switch (see Videos your browser cannot play). Conversions are capped at 720 lines, so turning this on also means watching a 4K video at 720p. The first time you play a video that is being converted, it is converted as it plays. A conversion happening live has no known length, so that first play has no duration and cannot be sought — the scrub bar and the seek shortcuts do nothing, and the player says so. Once you are done watching, that same conversion is written to a file in the background — afterwards rather than at the same time, so it never slows down the video you are watching — and every later play of that video is served from it: an ordinary video with a duration, a working scrub bar and working seek keys. Converted copies are kept under protected_media/transcoded/ and cost somewhere between 10 and 20 MB per minute of video, depending on how much movement there is in it. The store is capped and prunes the videos you have not watched for longest; an administrator can change the ceiling, or turn the whole thing off, with TRANSCODE_CACHE_MAX_GB.

These switches tell the captioning model what LibrePhotos already knows about a photo, so the caption can say who is in it and where it was taken. All are on by default. Tell the captioning model what LibrePhotos knows about a photo turns the context on. Default On Use the names of recognised people in captions includes the name of a recognised person in the prompt so it can appear in the caption. Only available while the switch above is on. Default On Mention where the photo was taken in captions includes the photo's geocoded location in the prompt. Only available while the switch above is on. Default On See Image Captioning for the captioning model itself.

Default slideshow interval sets the time in seconds between photos when using slideshow mode in the lightbox. New in 1.5.0 Show what's new after updates After LibrePhotos is updated, a small What's new card shows the highlights of the new version once, in the corner of the first page you open. Turn it off to never see the card. Account menu > What's new shows the highlights at any time either way. Default On. See The What's new card.

Most of these settings control how face clustering groups the faces in your library, which is what you work with when labelling people. How sure a suggested match must be is set on the face dashboard with Confidence in its Filter, not here. New in 1.5.0 Minimum face size skips the faces the face detector finds that are smaller than a share of the photo's shorter side, such as strangers far in the background or faces in a crowd. Options are Off, 2%, 4% and 8%; next to them, an example photo marks with a dashed red box the faces a choice skips, and the line under them says what it means in pixels (4% is under 43 px on a 1080 px tall photo). It applies to photos scanned from now on: faces found already stay (delete them on the face dashboard), and face regions saved in the file and faces you draw by hand are always kept. Default Off. Minimum cluster size changes how clusters form; a smaller value results in more clusters. Options are Auto, 2, 4, 8 and 16. Default Auto, which lets LibrePhotos choose for you. Minimum samples changes how conservative clustering is; a smaller value is less conservative. Options are 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16. Default 1 Cluster selection epsilon merges clusters whose faces are this close; a higher value merges more of one person's clusters, and Very high can also join look-alikes such as siblings. Options are Off (0), Small (0.9), Normal (0.95), High (1.0) and Very high (1.05), distances between face encodings scaled to length 1 (two photos of one person are about 0.9 apart). Default Normal. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0 the options were 0.025 to 0.2, too small to merge anything at all. A saved choice keeps its name when you update. Write face tags to image files when enabled, a photo's faces are written as XMP MWG-RS region tags to a sidecar file or to your image files, as chosen under Write edits to files, whenever you label, add, delete or restore a face (with that setting Off the switch is disabled and nothing is written), so face data stays portable across apps like Lightroom, digiKam and XnView. The names of the people are added to the photo's keywords. See Face regions. Default Off

These switches decide what public links show. Photo links always use them, including links you already created, so turning one off hides that detail on every public photo link at once. Album links use them unless the album's own link settings override them. All are off by default. Share photo timestamps: show when photos were taken. Share location information: show where photos were taken. Share camera information: show the camera make, model and settings. Share captions: show photo descriptions. Share detected faces: show the people recognised in photos. New in 1.5.0 While the admin has the public gallery open, a Public gallery card follows: Show my public photos in the public gallery (off by default) puts your public photos on the server's front page next to everyone else's. Next to it, What visitors see of your photos lists what the gallery shows, from the switches above. New in 1.5.0 Up to 1.4.0, these switches were not saved: after Save Changes they were off again on the next visit, and public links shared none of these details unless an album link turned them on.

These are your personal defaults for the Detection options dropdown on the Duplicates page — they pre-fill that dropdown before you click Detect duplicates, rather than running anything on their own. See Duplicate detection for the review workflow. The Visual sensitivity default controls how aggressively visual duplicates are matched: Strict (fewest matches, highest confidence), Normal (the balanced default) or Loose (most matches, but may include false positives). Default Normal The Clear pending duplicates default determines whether previously pending duplicate results are cleared before a new detection run starts. Default Off
These are settings that apply to the whole instance. Besides the panels below, the Admin area also hosts the Services and Server logs panels, documented in Library Management.

Allow user registration will enable a sign up button on the login page. Allow uploads sets if uploading should be possible or not New in 1.5.0 Single sign-on A group with the switches for logging in through an OpenID Connect identity provider: Show the single sign-on button, Button label and Allow sign-ups over single sign-on. It lists the providers set up in the Django admin and warns when SSO cannot work yet. See Single sign-on. New in 1.5.0 Check for new releases On by default. Once a day the backend asks github.com which LibrePhotos release is the newest; nothing about your server is sent. A line under the switch says what the last check found: up to date, a newer release (or that you skipped it, with Show it again), that the check failed, or that it is off. It is locked off when the server's UPDATE_CHECK environment variable is false, and development builds have nothing to compare. See Checking for new releases and The Update available card. New in 1.5.0 Show users what's new after an update On by default. After an update, each user sees a small What's new card once with the highlights of the new version, which are part of the app: nothing is downloaded. Turn it off to hide the card for everyone; each user can also turn it off for themselves under Settings > Interface. See The What's new card. New in 1.6.0 Ask admins to support LibrePhotos On by default. Once, when an admin's library has been scanned and processed for the first time, a thank-you dialog shows what LibrePhotos found, what the same storage would cost in Google One or iCloud+, and links to star the project on GitHub, sponsor it or donate through PayPal. Closing it, or opening one of its links, hides it for good. Rewind's last slide asks admins too. Other users are never asked for money: their Rewind ends with a link to star the project. Turn it off to never ask admins either. New in 1.6.0 Show Rewind around Christmas On by default. Between 20 December and 6 January, each user sees their Rewind once: their year in photos (how many they took, their busiest day and month, the people and places they photographed most), worked out on your server from their own photos. It does not open by itself for a year with fewer than 10 photos. During that time Account menu > Your Rewind opens it either way. Turn it off to keep it from opening by itself. Skip patterns Comma delimited list of patterns to ignore (e.g. '@eaDir,#recycle' for synology devices) New in 1.4.0 Missing photos limit The largest share of one user's photos that a scan may mark missing at once. Default 50%. When more than this share of the photos, and more than 100 photos, would lose all their files, the scan changes nothing and its job fails with "... photos would be marked missing. Nothing was changed. Is the library mounted?". This protects the library when a disk or share is not mounted (see Missing Photos). If you really removed most of a library, set it to 100% (off), scan, and set it back. New in 1.4.0 Scan libraries automatically Scans every user's library for new and changed files on a schedule: Off (the default), Every hour, Every day at a time, or Custom days at a time, in the server's time zone. A user whose scan is still running is skipped, so scans never pile up. A line under the setting says what the last run did and when the next one is. See Auto scan. New in 1.4.0 Delete photos from the trash after Days a photo stays in a user's trash before a daily task deletes it for good, together with its original files on disk. Default 0, which never deletes anything on its own. Turning it on or shortening it first asks, with the number of photos the next cleanup would delete. See Trash. Map provider Select which geocoding service converts GPS coordinates into place names. Options are Nominatim (free, no key required), Mapbox, MapTiler, OpenCage, and TomTom. API key for map provider Only shown after you select a commercial provider (Mapbox, MapTiler, OpenCage, or TomTom), where it is required. It is not shown for Nominatim, which needs no key. Map tiles Where the map background is loaded from. Options are PhotoPrism (the default), OpenStreetMap, or None to hide maps entirely. Opening a map reveals the approximate location of your photos to the selected provider. This is separate from the map provider above, which only affects reverse geocoding. Captioning model LFM2.5-VL (the default) or None to turn automatic captioning off. See Image Captioning. Text recognition (OCR) model None (the default) keeps text recognition off. PP-OCRv6 Tiny, PP-OCRv6 Small or PP-OCRv6 Medium turn it on, after a confirmation, because all readable text of every photo is then stored in the database. New in 1.5.0 The next scan or upload then starts reading the whole library. See Text Recognition (OCR). Face recognition model Select which InsightFace model is used to detect and recognise faces. Options: buffalo_sc — Lightweight model (default). Fastest and smallest, a good fit for most setups. buffalo_s / buffalo_m / buffalo_l — Progressively larger and more accurate, at the cost of more memory and compute. antelopev2 — High-accuracy model for the best recognition quality. Saving a new model queues a Download models job immediately (if the model pack is not already present). Only faces encoded after the switch use the new model — existing faces keep the embeddings they were created with. Train faces does not re-encode them; it only generates embeddings for faces that have none yet and then re-clusters. For this reason, choose a model before your first face scan: switching later leaves your library comparing embeddings produced by two different models. See Face recognition.

New in 1.5.0 The Public gallery card decides who the public gallery is open to: one page of the public photos of every user who takes part, at your server's address. Off (the default): there is no gallery. The server's address opens the login page, and the gallery's pages and API answer "not found". Members only: every signed-in user finds the gallery under Sharing, and sees it exactly as a visitor would. Use it to try the gallery out before anyone outside sees it. Everyone: the server's address opens the gallery for anyone who is not signed in, without an account. Log in stays in its top right corner. Opening it to more people first asks, with how many photos of how many users it shows and the names of the users with the most photos. Users take part only after they turn on Show my public photos in the public gallery in their settings; nobody does by default. Their public photos stay public either way, on their own links. Let search engines index the public gallery: Off by default. While it is off, the gallery's page and answers ask search engines not to list them (noindex): the API answers and, with the unified image and the Windows app, the page itself carry an X-Robots-Tag header. With the separate frontend container of the default Docker Compose setup, the page says it in a robots meta tag that its script adds, which search engines that run scripts read; a reverse proxy in front can add X-Robots-Tag: noindex for / and /public as well. The gallery is rate limited per user and, without an account, per address by PUBLIC_GALLERY_THROTTLE_RATE (see Rate limits).

New in 1.4.0 Below the Site settings card, the Features card has one switch per optional feature: Face detection, Face clustering, Image captioning, Things, Place names and Videos. Switch off what you do not need to make scans faster; what a feature already made (faces, names, captions, Things, place names) stays. A switch saves at once. A switch that the server's FEATURE_* environment variable turned off is disabled and marked Locked. For a feature that runs on a model, a line under the switch says whether the model is ready or shows its download. See Feature Toggles.

Below the Features card is an Email (SMTP) card that configures outgoing e-mail. Outgoing e-mail must be set up here, or the Forgot your password? flow silently does nothing (the server logs the failure but never reveals whether an address exists). Provider chooses how mail is sent: Disabled, Custom SMTP server, SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Brevo, SMTP2GO or Amazon SES. The hosted providers use built-in server presets, so you only supply a From address, Username and API key. Custom SMTP server (and Amazon SES, for the host) additionally shows the SMTP host; Custom SMTP server also shows Port, Use STARTTLS and Use implicit SSL. From address is the address mail is sent from. Username is the login for the provider. For SendGrid, leave this blank — it uses the literal username apikey. Password / API key is write-only: it is encrypted before it is stored and never returned by the API. Leaving the field blank keeps the existing credential unchanged; use Remove the stored credential to delete it (it asks first, since most providers refuse to send mail, password reset links included, until a credential is entered again). Send test email sends a test message to your own account's e-mail address to check the configuration end to end. It stays disabled until the configuration is valid.

Delete all auto created albums removes every automatically generated event album in one step. Your photos are not affected. Download server stats saves a serverstats.json report — see Server Stats for what it contains. Remove photo details from old thumbnails starts a job that removes the location and other photo details from thumbnails made by LibrePhotos 1.2.1 or older. Your photos are not changed. While it runs, the row shows how far it got and links to the job. See After upgrading from 1.2.1 or older. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, this tool was not in the Admin area. Look up place names again asks the current Map provider for the place of every photo with a location, for every user, after a confirmation, for example after switching to ExifTool. Places albums under the old names end up empty. With an online provider it can take hours. See Switching the provider. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, switching the provider never renamed photos already named.

The admin can change here the scan directory, upload folder and password for users, or add new users to the system. Deleting a user keeps their photos and albums under a placeholder account, turns off their public links and removes nothing from disk. See Managing users.
Shows how far jobs are progressed. For more information, go here

Most images have metadata for dates, but these are split in multiple places and around 10-20% of "real world" photos have incomplete data metadata. The configurable date time parser allows us to get these dates and display them nicely as the user wants it too.

The logic for extracting local time is described as a list of rules that should be applied one after another until one rule is able to extract date time (or until all rules are tried without success). If a rule can't fetch the time (e.g. the EXIF tag value is not present or the path doesn't match the rule) then that rule is considered to be not applicable.

A date you set by hand in a photo's info panel, or for many photos at once with Change date and time…, is not a rule: it always wins over every rule in the list, on every scan and rescan, however you order or edit your rules. The info panel says Set by you under such a date.
