While you drag, the whole window shows where the files will go: Drop photos and videos to upload, or Add to the running upload when an upload is already in progress, in which case the new files join the end of the queue. On the profile page, dropping an image on your avatar still sets your avatar instead.

New in 1.4.0 You can upload straight into one of your own albums, so new photos land in the album without being added to it afterwards: On the album's page, open the ⋮ at the right of its header and choose Upload to this album…, then pick the files. Or drag files onto the album's page. The overlay then says Drop to add to and the album's name. An empty album shows a drop zone with an Upload photos button. Use New album on My albums to make an empty album to upload into (see Albums). The files go to your upload folder and your library as usual, and are added to the album as soon as each one is imported. The upload card names the album (Adding to Porto 2025) and, when it is done, says how many files were added, with an Open album link. A file that is already in your library is not uploaded again but is added to the album; its row says Already in your library: added to the album. A locked album takes no uploads: its menu item says why, and files dropped on its page go to your library only. If an album is locked or deleted while its upload runs, the remaining files go to your library only and their rows say so. Only your own albums take uploads, not albums others share with you.

We accept all files that have a mime type of image or video, plus HEIC, HEIF, JPEG XL, AVIF and camera RAW files (.arw, .cr3, .dng, .nef, ...), which some browsers hand over without a mime type. If you drag other files along (a PDF, for example), the overlay says Only photos and videos can be uploaded, and only the photos and videos are uploaded.
documents.s: What kinds of files are supported?

documents.t: While files upload, a card in the bottom right corner lists them with their status. Uploads run one file at a time, and the card stays while you browse other pages. New in 1.4.0 Cancel in the card stops the upload. The file being sent stops after its current 1 MB chunk, and every file that was not uploaded yet is marked Cancelled. Files that already finished stay in your library. Retry in the card uploads the cancelled and failed files again, as long as the tab is open. Closing or reloading the tab while an upload runs asks first, with your browser's own Leave site? dialog. Moving to another page inside LibrePhotos does not stop the upload. Logging out while an upload runs asks first too: Stop and log out cancels the upload, Keep uploading keeps it going. A cancelled or abandoned upload leaves a partial file on the server. A daily cleanup on the server deletes it once it got no new data for a day. python manage.py delete_expired_uploads does the same by hand. Not released yet (comes after 1.6.0) Up to 1.6.0 the day counted from the start of the upload, so a very long upload could be deleted while it was still running.
documents.s: Following, cancelling and leaving an upload

documents.t: New in 1.5.0 Sending the files is only the first half: the server then makes their thumbnails, reads their dates and looks for things, places and faces. The card follows that too, so it no longer says Upload complete before your photos are in the timeline: Processing your uploads with 12/40 ready: the bar turns two-tone, green for the photos that are ready and blue for those uploaded and still being processed. Each file's row goes from Uploading to Processing to Ready, and a ready row shows the photo's thumbnail. The count includes uploads from the mobile app made at the same time, since the server imports them together. The timeline fills in as photos become ready; you do not have to reload. Updating search and faces: every photo is in the timeline, and the server is now making them searchable by content and grouping their faces. 38 photos ready, with how many files were uploaded and how many were already in your library. A file the server could not read (an unsupported RAW format, a damaged file) says Not imported on its own row, with the reason and a link to My jobs. A photo that is in your library but one of the later steps failed for (finding faces, for example) is Ready with a note naming the step. If the server makes no progress for two minutes, for example because a scan is running, the card says so; your files are safe and are processed once the server gets to them. You can close the card while the server works. As long as uploads are being imported, from this browser or from the mobile app, the ring around your avatar shows it and the account menu has an Importing your uploads section with the same count. It runs next to other jobs, so Scan stays available, and it cannot be cancelled. An empty timeline says Importing your uploads instead of asking you to scan. Up to 1.4.0 the card said Upload complete as soon as the files were sent, and the timeline was refreshed before the photos had thumbnails.
documents.s: After the upload: processing on the server

documents.t: The upload process works in the following way: Check if file is on the server by comparing the hash md5 + user_id If it is, don't upload it (when uploading into an album, the photo you already have is added to the album instead) If it isn't, upload it We upload files in 1MB chunks When each file finishes uploading, the backend registers that one photo, counts it in your Import uploads job and queues its processing (metadata and thumbnails, then adding it to the album it was uploaded into, caption, geolocation, album dates, face extraction). No directory scan is triggered. New in 1.5.0 When the last file is sent, the web app tells the server the upload is over (POST /api/upload/seal/), and follows the import with GET /api/upload/status/ (see the upload API). An upload into an album sends the album's id with the last request (album_id on /api/upload/complete/). The server checks that the album is yours and not locked before it saves the file; otherwise it answers 400 with the code album_not_found or album_locked, and the web app completes the same upload again without the album.

The upload behavior depends on whether the user has a scan directory configured: When scan directory is properly configured:​ Files are saved to: {scan_directory}/uploads/web/{filename}, also when the mobile app backs them up This is the normal and expected behavior Files are stored in the mounted host directory and are persistent An admin can point a user's uploads at a different folder with the Upload folder field in the user edit dialog (see Managing users). Files then go to {upload folder}/web/{filename} instead. When scan directory is NOT configured:​ Uploads are blocked and nothing is written to disk. If your account has no scan directory set, the upload button is disabled and shows the tooltip "Scan directory not configured - contact administrator". Files dragged onto the app are not uploaded; the overlay says Uploading is not set up yet. If a scan directory is set but the path does not exist on the server, the button stays active, but the upload is rejected once the final chunk is submitted. In both cases the API responds with HTTP 400 — "Upload failed: No scan directory configured…" or "Upload failed: Scan directory '<path>' does not exist…" — and no file is saved.

To use the upload feature properly, you must have: Upload feature enabled: Turn on Allow uploads in the admin area. Docker Compose users can pre-enable it by adding allowUpload=true to their .env before the first start — Compose passes it to the backend as ALLOW_UPLOAD (note the variable in .env is allowUpload, not ALLOW_UPLOAD) Scan directory configured: Every user must have a scan directory set up by an admin

Admin users only: Only admins can set scan directories for users Access admin panel: Click on your avatar (top right) → Admin area Set scan directory: Manually set the Scan Directory for each user Verify path: The directory must exist and be accessible to the container

You can activate / deactivate by navigating as an admin to the admin area and clicking on the Allow uploads switch. This switch is the authoritative setting. The ALLOW_UPLOAD environment variable (set through allowUpload in your .env for the Docker Compose deployment) only supplies the initial default: once a value has been saved to the database — by toggling the switch, or by the first-time setup wizard — the stored setting wins and the environment variable is ignored.

After upload, you can scan the uploaded photos in two ways: Automatic scanning: The upload process automatically triggers processing for the uploaded photo Manual scanning: You can manually scan all uploaded photos by going to the Library page and clicking the scan button. That scan covers your scan directory, so it does not reach an upload folder an admin set outside it.

Upload button is greyed out​ Cause: Your account has no scan directory configured. Hovering the button shows "Scan directory not configured - contact administrator". Solution: Ask an admin to set your scan directory (see How to configure scan directory). Upload fails with "Scan directory does not exist"​ Cause: The configured scan directory path is not present inside the backend container. Solution: Check that the path matches the ${scanDirectory}:/data bind mount in your compose file, and that the directory exists on the host. Uploaded files disappear after container restart​ Cause: The data root is not backed by a host directory. A scan directory has to live inside the backend's data root (/data by default) — anything outside it is rejected with "Scan directory must be inside the data root." — so the upload itself succeeds, but if /data is not bind-mounted, everything written there lives only in the container's filesystem and is lost when the container is recreated. Solution: Make sure your compose file mounts a host directory at /data (the ${scanDirectory}:/data line on the backend service) and that scanDirectory in your .env points at a real, persistent path on the host. Upload fails with permission errors​ Cause: The container doesn't have write permissions to the scan directory. Solution: Check the directory permissions and ensure the container can write to the mounted directory. Upload button not visible​ Cause: Upload feature is disabled. Solution: Toggle Allow uploads on in the admin area. Note that the allowUpload environment variable only supplies the default value: once the setting has been saved from the admin area or the first-run setup wizard, the value lives in the database and changing the env var has no effect.

LibrePhotos provides several ways to browse your photo library. You can switch between views using the sidebar (the tabs at the bottom of the screen on a phone) or the dropdown in the title of the Photos page, which also holds Favorites, Videos, Hidden, Archive and the other views below.

The default view showing all your photos grouped by date, from newest to oldest. A scroll scrubber on the right edge lets you quickly jump to any date — click or drag it to navigate through large libraries. Newest or oldest first​ New in 1.5.0 Up to 1.4.0, every list was newest first. To read your photos the way they happened, for example a holiday from the first day to the last, pick Oldest first under Order in the view options (View options… in the ⋯ at the right of the page header, or the View options button on a page with no other actions). The order is by date taken, not by when a photo was added, and it changes nothing on your photos or in your albums. It is saved to your account, so your other devices and browsers follow it, and it applies to every list grouped by day: the timeline and the Favorites, Photos, Videos, Screenshots, Documents, Hidden, Archive and Trash views, your albums and the albums shared with you, people, places, things, tags and folders, search results grouped by day (semantic search results stay in order of relevance), a shared library's timeline and public pages you open while signed in. Visitors without an account see public pages newest first. The photos within a day follow the same order, and the scroll scrubber turns round with the list: its top is your oldest year. Photos without a date stay at the end in both orders. While the order is oldest first, the line under the page title ends with Oldest first. Events always read oldest first, as they happened: on an event the Order control shows that and cannot be changed. Scroll bar style​ New in 1.5.0 The scroll scrubber appears when you point at the right edge or scroll a long way, and runs from just under the header to the bottom of the window. Pick how it looks under Scroll bar in the view options (View options… in the ⋯ at the right of the page header). The choice is saved to your account and applies to every photo list: Simple: a thin track with a handle you can drag. A bubble next to the handle shows the date you are at, and the years (or months) appear beside the track while you point at it. Photo density: one bar per month, as wide as the number of photos in it, so busy trips and quiet years stand out. A frame marks the part you are looking at, and pointing at a bar shows its month and how many photos it holds. Very long timelines show one bar per year instead. Click a year or month label to jump there. Filtering the timeline​ New in 1.3.0 The Filter button in the page header narrows what the timeline shows. On a phone it is an icon, and the filter opens as a sheet from the bottom of the screen: Media type: all, photos only, or videos only. Hide from timeline: leave out Screenshots and/or Documents (see Fixing a wrong category). Show only: Favorites. While a filter is active the button is highlighted with the number of active filters, and the header says what is filtered. The filter lives in the page address, so it survives a reload and can be bookmarked. Save as default makes the current filter what the timeline shows every time you open it, for example to keep screenshots out for good. Reset to default goes back to your saved default. A saved default applies to the main timeline only: Favorites, Screenshots, Videos, Hidden, Trash, albums, folders, search, people, places and public pages are never filtered by it. Selecting all photos on a filtered timeline selects only what it shows, so Select all followed by Move to trash never reaches the screenshots or documents the filter hides.

Photos you've marked as favorites. To favorite a photo, click the star icon in the lightbox toolbar (or press f), or use the selection actions menu. The star turns yellow once the photo's rating reaches the Minimum image rating to interpret as favorite value in your user settings. Removing a favorite sets the photo's rating to 0, which also clears a star rating it had (for example a 5-star rating imported from Lightroom or digiKam). If you rate with stars, switch to stars mode instead. Rating photos with stars​ New in 1.4.0 Set Rating style to Stars in Settings to rate photos from 1 to 5 stars instead of marking favorites: In the photo viewer, five stars replace the favorite star in the toolbar, and on the photo page a Rating tile replaces Favorite. Click a star to set the rating, click the current rating again to clear it, or press 1 to 5 (0 clears it). On a photo someone shared with you, the stars show the owner's rating and cannot be changed. In the grid, a rated photo shows its rating, such as 4 ★, in the top-right corner. Unrated photos show nothing. To rate several photos, select them and choose Set rating from the selection actions menu. Set rating is not available after Select all: select the photos one by one instead. The rating is the same 0-5 rating that is read from and written to the file's metadata, so it matches what the mobile app and other photo tools show. Photos at or above Minimum image rating to interpret as favorite still appear on the Favorites page.

Photos you've hidden. Hiding a photo takes it out of every view (the timeline, albums, people, places, search and folders) without deleting it; this page is the only place it still shows. To hide photos, select them and choose "Hide" from the selection actions menu. To keep a photo in your albums but off the timeline, archive it instead (see Hidden or archived?).

Photos you've archived. Archiving takes a photo off the main timeline and out of Memories, and nothing else: it stays in its albums, on the people and places pages, in folders and in search. Use it for photos you have sorted into albums and no longer want to scroll past, or for receipts and other photos you want to keep but not see every day. To archive photos, select them and choose Archive from the selection actions menu (the ⋮ button). Unarchive in the same menu puts them back on the timeline. Both work after Select all too. In the photo viewer, Archive photo in the ⋮ (More actions), or the a key, archives the photo you are looking at, or unarchives it. On the photo page it is under More. Open the Archive page from the Photos header dropdown (after Hidden) or by searching for "Archive" with Ctrl + k. It has the same media filter as the Hidden page. In albums, search and the other views, an archived photo has a small archive mark in its top right corner, so you can see why it is not on your timeline. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, photos could not be archived. Hidden or archived?​ Where the photo shows Archived Hidden Timeline (Photos) No No Memories No No Albums, events Yes No People, places, things, tags Yes No Search Yes No Folders Yes No Favorites, Videos, Screenshots and the other views in the Photos dropdown Yes No Its own page Archive Hidden A photo can be hidden and archived at the same time; then it is hidden, and shows only on the Hidden page until you unhide it. Neither one deletes the photo or changes its file.

Shows only your most recent batch of imports — the photos whose added date falls on the same calendar day as the most recently added photo in your library. They appear in a single flat grid under one "Added on …" line in the page header; there is no per-day grouping. Older imports are not listed here — use the Timeline to browse your whole library. With a media filter, the page shows the latest day a matching photo was added, for example the last day you imported videos.
Shows only still photos, filtering out all videos.
Shows only video files, filtering out all still photos.

Screenshots lists the photos detected or marked as screenshots. Documents lists the photos of receipts, letters, forms and other paper (see Documents). Both are in the Photos view switcher in the page header and in the command palette (Ctrl+K). When a photo is in the wrong one, change its Category. Note New in 1.4.0 This applies to the Documents page.

Note New in 1.4.0 This applies to the labelled media button, its Documents only choice, and the filter on Trash, Recently Added, Without Timestamp, Without Location and folder pages. Favorites, Hidden, Trash, Recently Added, Without Timestamp, Without Location, Not in an Album, search results, and the album, person, place, thing, tag and folder pages have a media button in the page header. It names what the page shows: All media, Photos only, Videos only, Screenshots only or Documents only. Click it to pick another. While a filter is on, the button is highlighted, the header says what the page shows, and Show all next to it goes back to all media. On a phone the button is an icon with a dot while a filter is on. The choice is part of the page address (for example ?media=videos), so it survives a reload and can be bookmarked. Every page starts with all media: the saved default of the timeline filter never applies here. Selecting all photos on a filtered list selects only what it shows. In Trash, filter to Videos only, then Select all and Delete permanently removes the trashed videos and leaves every other photo in the trash.
documents.s: Filtering a list by media type

documents.t: Photos that don't have a date/time in their EXIF metadata. Useful for finding and fixing photos with missing timestamps. New in 1.4.0 To give them a date, select them and choose Edit info → Change date and time… from the selection actions menu, then Set (see Changing the date of many photos).

New in 1.4.0 Photos that have no GPS coordinates, oldest added first. Open a photo and set its location from the Location section of the details sidebar; once it has coordinates it leaves this view. A photo whose coordinates could not be turned into a place name still has a location, so it is not listed here. To give many of them one place, select them and choose Edit info → Set location… from the selection actions menu (see Setting the location of many photos). Select all reaches every photo on the page, not only the ones loaded so far, and the page has the media filter.

New in 1.4.0 Your photos that are in none of your own albums, newest first, so you can see what is left to sort. An album another user shares with you does not count: a photo of yours that is only in their album still shows up here. Hidden and trashed photos are left out. Open it from the Photos view switcher in the page header (under Without Timestamp and Without Location) or from the command palette (Ctrl+K, "not in an album"). Select photos and add them to an album from the selection actions; they leave the list once it refreshes. Select all reaches every photo on the page, not only the ones loaded so far, and the page has the media filter.
Photos you've marked as publicly visible, accessible at your public profile URL.

Browse your photos by filesystem directory structure. The root view shows the subfolders of your scan directory, each with a count of the photos inside it (including photos in nested subfolders). Click into any folder to see its photos and subfolders. Only folders that contain indexed photos are listed — folders that are empty, hidden (names starting with .), or not yet scanned will not appear.

When you click on any photo in LibrePhotos, it opens in the photo viewer (also known as the lightbox). This provides a full-screen view of your photo with navigation controls and a details sidebar. The photo sits on a plain black background in light and dark mode, so nothing of the page behind it changes how its colours and exposure look. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, the page showed through a dimmed, blurred layer around the photo.
Arrow keys or swipe to navigate between photos Thumbnail bar at the bottom shows nearby photos for quick navigation Close button (X) or press Escape to return to the gallery

The open photo is part of the page's address, as ?photo=<id> (for example /favorites?photo=<id> or /album/user/12?photo=<id>). New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, opening a photo left the address as it was. That gives you: Back in the browser, or the back gesture on a phone, closes the photo and leaves the grid where it was, scrolled to the photo you looked at last. Stepping to the next or previous photo does not add a step to the history, so one Back always closes the viewer. Reload reopens the same photo. A link to this photo in this view: copy the address while the photo is open. Whoever opens it sees the same page with that photo open, and can step through the rest of the list from there. A photo the list does not hold (on a page of the timeline that has not loaded yet, or hidden by a filter) opens on its own, without previous and next. A photo the person may not see, or that no longer exists, leaves the grid as it is. On a public album the same works for visitors, as long as the photo is in the album. The photo page at /photo/<id> is a separate page for one photo, without the list around it.

The toolbar at the top starts with the back arrow (Close), which returns to the gallery, followed by the photo's date and place. On the right, from left to right: 360° view - New in 1.5.0 Look around in a 360° photo sphere instead of seeing it flat. Shown only for photo spheres. Select text in photo - Lay the recognised text over the photo so you can select and copy it. Shown only on your own photos where text recognition found text. Share link (share icon) - Create a revocable link to this one photo and show it with a copy button, plus Replace link and Revoke. The icon is green while the photo has a live link. This does not make the photo public; see Revocable Photo Links. Edit - Not released yet (comes after 1.6.0) Open the photo editor to crop, straighten and adjust the photo. Your own still photos only. The button is highlighted on a photo you edited. Favorite (star icon) - Mark the photo as a favorite, or remove the mark. In stars mode this is a row of five stars instead (see Rating photos with stars). Show info panel / Hide info panel - Show or hide the photo details sidebar. Delete photo (trash icon) - Move the photo to trash. On a photo in the trash it is Restore photo. More actions (⋮) - A menu with the rest: Zoom in / Zoom out - Magnify the image. Still photos only, not videos. See Zooming into the original. Slideshow / Stop slideshow - Start or stop an automatic slideshow. While it runs, the toolbar shows its controls, with a dropdown to choose the interval (3, 5, 10, 15 or 30 seconds). Copy to clipboard - Copy the photo as an image to your clipboard, ready to paste into a chat, a document or an email. It copies the display-size version the viewer shows; use Download for the original file. It is offered for still photos, and only when LibrePhotos is served over HTTPS, because browsers allow clipboard access on secure pages only. Fullscreen / Exit fullscreen - Enter or leave fullscreen mode for distraction-free viewing. Hide photo / Unhide photo - Hide the photo everywhere but the Hidden page, or unhide it. Archive photo / Unarchive photo - Take the photo off the timeline and Memories, or put it back (see Archive). Rotate 90° counter-clockwise / Rotate 90° clockwise - Rotate the photo 90° in either direction (see Rotating Photos). Rescan file and Detect faces again, under Files (see Library Management and Face recognition). Each item in the menu shows its keyboard shortcut (see Keyboard Shortcuts). On a phone, Share link, the info panel button and Delete photo sit in a bar at the bottom of the screen instead of the top. New in 1.6.0 Up to 1.5.x, zoom, the slideshow, copy, fullscreen, hide, archive and the rotations had buttons of their own in the toolbar on a wide screen, and the share link button was a globe. The share link, favorite, delete, hide, archive and rotate controls are only shown when you are signed in. On a public or shared album page the toolbar shows just the zoom, slideshow, copy and fullscreen items in the ⋮, the info panel button and the back arrow. There is no download button in the lightbox itself (only the Original link on the zoom label of a RAW or other preview). To download photos, select them in the gallery grid and choose Download from the selection actions menu; the download dialog can also include the other photos from each selected photo's stack. To share photos with other users, select them in the grid and choose Sharing from the same menu. Not released yet (comes after 1.6.0) On a photo you edited, the ⋮ also has Download edited and Download original. To put a single photo on the clipboard, open it and press the Copy to clipboard button or Ctrl + c (⌘ + c on macOS). The browser's own right-click menu on the picture offers Copy image as well.

New in 1.5.0 The viewer shows a display-size version of each photo, 1080 pixels high by default. When you zoom in (Zoom in in the viewer's ⋮, a double-click, z or a pinch), it loads the original file in the background and switches to it once it is there, so the details stay sharp. Up to 1.4.0, zooming only enlarged the display-size version. A small label in the photo's lower-left corner says what you are looking at while you are zoomed in: Loading original while the file is on its way. The display-size version stays on screen until then. Original · 6000 × 4000 once the original is shown, which shrinks to Original after two seconds. The viewer keeps the original until you move to another photo. Preview with the reason when the browser cannot show the original: RAW, HEIC, TIFF and JPEG XL files, and photos you turned with the rotate buttons (the file itself is not turned). The Original link next to it downloads the file. The original did not load with Try again when loading it failed. Not released yet (comes after 1.6.0) On a photo you edited, zooming in loads the edited picture at full size, and the label says so: Loading the edited photo, then Edited · 3000 × 2000, which shrinks to Edited. While the server is still making it, the label says Preview with The edited photo is still being prepared at full size, without an Original link: the original file is Download original in the viewer's ⋮. Photos no bigger than the display-size version need nothing more, and animated GIFs always show the original. The original loads only when you are signed in and may download it anyway: your own photos and photos shared with you. Visitors of a public album or a public photo link keep the display-size version.

New in 1.5.0 A photo sphere is a 360° panorama: a phone's Photo Sphere or Panorama 360 mode, a 360° camera (Ricoh Theta, Insta360, GoPro Max) or a stitching program saves it as one picture twice as wide as tall. LibrePhotos marks one in the grid with a 360° badge in the lower right corner of its tile, and the viewer shows it flat, like any photo, until you ask for the 360° view: Press the 360° view button in the toolbar, or v. The photo becomes a sphere you are standing in: drag (or swipe) to look around, pinch or scroll to zoom. With the keyboard, the arrow keys look around and + and - zoom, so while the view is on, the arrow keys do not step to the next photo: use the arrows on the sides or the thumbnail bar, or leave the view first. The bar at the bottom of the sphere has Zoom out, Zoom in and Face forward, which turns back to the direction the photo was taken facing. Press 360° view again, v or Escape to see the photo flat again. The next photo always opens flat. The view loads the original file, so the sphere stays sharp when you zoom in; this can take a moment for a large panorama. It loads only when you turn the view on, so stepping through photo spheres costs no more than stepping through other photos. Where the original is not offered (visitors of a public album, a HEIC file, a photo you turned with the rotate buttons), the view uses the display-size version, which looks softer. The view does not turn by itself, and with Reduce motion set in your system it also stops at once when you let go. The 360° view needs WebGL. In a browser without it, the button stays visible, greyed out, and says so when you point at it or focus it. If a photo cannot be shown as a sphere, the viewer goes back to the flat photo and says so. Which photos are photo spheres: the scan reads the panorama information Google's Photo Sphere format puts in the file (GPano:ProjectionType is equirectangular; see what LibrePhotos reads). Phones, 360° cameras and most stitching programs write it. A photo without it counts as a sphere when it is exactly twice as wide as tall and at least 6000 pixels wide, which is what a stitched sphere without that information looks like; narrower ones are left flat, since some phones take photos twice as wide as tall. Flat panoramas (cylindrical) and 360° videos are not shown in the viewer. Photo spheres you added before 1.5.0 are found when they are scanned again: run a Rescan once after updating (on the Library page, in the dropdown next to Scan).

Rotate 90° counter-clockwise and Rotate 90° clockwise in the viewer's ⋮ (More actions) let you reorient a photo in 90° steps — useful for images that were captured at the wrong angle or whose EXIF Orientation tag is missing or incorrect. Rotation in LibrePhotos is non-destructive: The original image file on disk is not modified. Instead, the rotation is recorded as an EXIF Orientation override stored in the database, and the thumbnails are regenerated so the new orientation is visible everywhere in the UI. Each rotation composes on top of the previous one, so rotating clockwise twice produces a 180° rotation and four times returns the photo to its original orientation. The change applies to the photo for every viewer, not just your own session. Rotation is only available for still images. Videos cannot be rotated from the lightbox. Not released yet (comes after 1.6.0) On a photo you edited, the rotation turns the edit, crop included, and is added to the edit's history. Your Write edits to files setting (Settings → Metadata) controls whether the rotation also reaches the filesystem. This is a three-way choice, not an on/off toggle: Off, the default: only the LibrePhotos database and thumbnails are updated, and the file on disk stays byte-for-byte identical. Save to sidecar: the original stays untouched and the new orientation is written to the photo's XMP sidecar as XMP-tiff:Orientation, for every image format. Apps that take the orientation from a sidecar, such as digiKam, show the photo turned the same way (darktable ignores it). The value is relative to the image as stored in the file: for a HEIC or AVIF photo it starts from the file's own rotation (its irot and imir), not from its EXIF Orientation, which can disagree. Save to media file: for JPEG, PNG, TIFF and WebP files, LibrePhotos writes the new EXIF Orientation into the original, so every viewer shows the rotation. HEIC, AVIF, RAW and the other formats are not rewritten: their viewers ignore that tag, so the rotation stays in LibrePhotos. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0, a rotation never reached the sidecar, and Save to media file wrote a wrong EXIF Orientation into HEIC, AVIF and RAW originals (often the opposite turn), replacing the camera's own value. LibrePhotos' own thumbnails were not affected. If another app shows such a file turned the wrong way, set its orientation there or with exiftool -Orientation=....

The sidebar displays detailed information about the current photo and provides quick access to related content. New in 1.4.0 While you edit the date, the caption, the tags or the location, a dimmed line under the editor says where the change is kept: Saved in LibrePhotos only, or Saved in LibrePhotos and written to the sidecar file (or to the photo file). It follows your Write edits to files setting, which its Settings link opens. All four are written to files.

New in 1.4.0 An edit is kept only once you save it: the check (✓) of the date, caption and tags editors, or Save in the location picker. While the date, caption or tags you typed differ from what is saved, an orange Unsaved mark sits next to that editor's title. With such an edit, or a spot picked in the location picker and not saved yet, stepping to another photo (with the arrows, the arrow keys or a swipe), picking a stack or similar photo, closing the viewer, or going Back then asks Discard unsaved changes? first: Keep editing leaves you where you were with your text intact, Discard drops the edit and goes on. An editor you opened but did not change never asks. On the photo page, leaving with an unsaved edit asks Leave without saving?, and reloading or closing the tab asks through the browser's own dialog in both places.

Shows when the photo was taken. You can click the edit button to modify the date and time if needed. Save stays greyed out while the time field is empty or incomplete, and the editor stays open until the date is saved; if the save fails, LibrePhotos says so and your input is kept. After a save, an Undo timestamp modification button next to the date puts the previous date back. New in 1.4.0 A date you set this way wins over the date rules and is marked Set by you. To drop it, edit the date and click Remove timestamp: the date rules decide the photo's date again, so it keeps a date read from its file if it has one.

New in 1.4.0 A camera with a wrong clock, or one left on summer time, puts a whole trip off by the same amount. To fix it, select the photos in the grid (or Select all), open the selection actions menu (⋮) and choose Edit info → Change date and time…. The dialog has two tabs: Shift moves every selected photo by the same amount, so their order and the time between them stay the same. Pick Earlier or Later and enter the days, hours, minutes and seconds, or click 1 h earlier or 1 h later. A line spells out the shift ("1 hour, 30 minutes earlier"), and a table shows the oldest and newest selected photo now and after the shift. Shift stays greyed out until the amount is more than zero. Photos without a date are left alone; the dialog says how many. Set gives every selected photo the same date and time, picked with the same calendar and time field as the Timestamp editor. Use it for scans and photos without a date. The photos then share one time, so their order on the timeline is lost. When you save, a message says how many photos got their new date and how many a shift skipped. The new dates count as set by you: they win over the date rules, a rescan keeps them, and Remove timestamp in a photo's Timestamp editor hands that photo back to the rules. With Write edits to files on, LibrePhotos writes them to the photos' files or sidecars in the background, as XMP:DateCreated.
documents.s: Changing the date of many photos

documents.t: Near the top of the sidebar, LibrePhotos shows a summary of the current file: the filename (a link that opens the original file in a new tab), the image dimensions, megapixels and file size (for a video: its dimensions, duration, codec and size), and, when the photo has more than one file, the +N formats toggle described under File Variants below. When the photo carries camera EXIF, two rows follow, as on a camera's own info screen: Camera: the camera's make and model, with the shutter speed, the ISO and the exposure bias (1/250 · ISO 200 · +0.7 EV). Lens: the lens, with the aperture and the focal length, plus its 35 mm equivalent when that differs (ƒ/5.6 · 23 mm (35 mm equiv.)). A row the photo has nothing for is left out; without a lens name, the aperture and focal length join the camera row. Numbers follow your interface language, so German shows ƒ/5,6 and 8,4 MB. A shutter speed of a quarter second or longer is given in seconds (2.5 s). Show more reveals the rest, with labels: whether the flash fired, the white balance, the metering mode, the subject distance and the digital zoom, then the folder of the file and any duplicate file copies. The button is not shown when there is nothing more. For the full list of EXIF fields, see EXIF Data. New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0 the camera and lens shared one line, without the exposure bias, the megapixels, the flash, white balance or metering mode.

If a photo has multiple file variants (e.g., RAW+JPEG pairs, Live Photos with embedded video, or edited copies), the file info row shows a +N formats toggle that lists them with type badges (JPG, RAW, VIDEO, META). Downloading a photo always includes every one of its file variants in the zip — there is no separate option for that. The download dialog's only checkbox, "Include all photos from stacks", controls whether the other photos from the same stack (bursts, brackets, manual stacks) are added as well. A RAW badge overlay is shown on photos that have RAW file variants. For more details on how file variants and stacks work, see Stacks & File Variants.

New in 1.3.0 LibrePhotos detects screenshots while scanning and documents (receipts, letters, forms) from their text, and the Classify media categories job (listed on the Jobs page) re-runs both over the library. The category is the badge at the end of the filename row in File & Camera Info. When it is wrong, click the badge and pick Photo, Screenshot or Document. The menu also says whether the category was Detected automatically or Set by you, and where the item appears with your saved timeline filter. A notification with Undo confirms the change; undoing a correction of a detected category hands the item back to the detectors. Videos get the badge only when they were wrongly flagged, and can only be set back to Photo. A category you set is kept: rescanning the library or running Classify media categories again never overwrites it. The control is shown on your own photos only. To fix many items at once, select them in the grid, open the selection actions menu (⋮) and choose Mark as, then Photo, Screenshot or Document.

Displays the location where the photo was taken (if GPS data is available). An interactive map shows where the shot was made — you can pan and zoom it with the on-map navigation controls, and clicking the marker opens a small popup with the photo's thumbnail. To set or correct a location, click the pencil icon next to the place name to open the Pick location dialog. (The pencil is hidden on publicly shared photos.) New in 1.4.0 On your own photos, the coordinates are shown under the place name (37.08990, -8.41280), with a button that copies them in that form for a map or a search box, and the altitude when the photo has one (31 m above sea level). The copy button needs HTTPS, like copying an image. People you share a photo with, and visitors of a public album, never see this line.

Shows faces detected in the photo. You can: Click on a face to view all photos of that person Edit the person's name by clicking the edit button Mark a face as "Not this person" if incorrectly identified

The AI-generated or manually entered caption for the photo. You can: View the things OpenCLIP detected, displayed as green badges under Things; click one to search for it Edit the caption manually — type # to get autocomplete suggestions for thing album tags Generate a new AI caption using the suggestion button Use the AI suggestion button to quickly fill in a machine-generated caption

Your own tags for the photo, shown as teal badges. This section always appears in the sidebar when you are signed in, showing No tags when none are set. Click the pencil button to open an editor where you can add or remove tags — separate entries with a comma, and existing tags are offered as autocomplete suggestions, the ones beginning with what you typed first — then use the check to save or the X to cancel. Click a tag badge to open that tag's album. Tags also come from the photo file: a scan turns each keyword stored in it (XMP Subject, IPTC Keywords, the PersonInImage names and the last level of each HierarchicalSubject keyword, including .xmp sidecars) into a tag. Those tags carry a small file icon, and hovering or focusing one says From the file's keywords. You edit them like any other tag. With Write edits to files set to Off, removing one here does not change the file, so a rescan adds it back, and the editor says so. With a sidecar or the media file chosen, your tag changes are written to the file's keywords (see EXIF Data). New in 1.4.0 A removed tag stays removed. Up to 1.3.0, the file's keywords showed in a separate Keywords section below the tags. These are not the same as the Things list under the caption: those come from OpenCLIP and are not editable here. To tag many photos in one go, select them in the grid and press t instead — see Tagging photos. Tags are not shown on public or shared album pages.

Shows which user albums contain this photo. Each album is displayed with: Cover photo thumbnail - A preview of the album's cover Album title - Click to navigate directly to that album Photo count - Number of photos in the album This makes it easy to see the context of a photo and quickly jump to related albums without leaving the photo viewer.

Displays photos that are visually similar to the current one. This is useful for: Finding duplicates Discovering related photos from the same event Browsing photos with similar content Click on any similar photo to view it directly.

Every photo also has a page of its own at /photo/<id>. You get there from a link to the photo, by Ctrl + clicking (⌘ + click on macOS) a photo in a grid, and from a similar photo in the details. Note New in 1.4.0 Up to 1.3.0 the page was titled with the file name and its full folder path and had no actions. The photo or video is shown as large as the window allows on a neutral background, with Back above it (to where you came from, or to the timeline when you opened a link) and Open in viewer below it. Open in viewer shows the photo in the lightbox, for zoom, fullscreen, the slideshow and the keyboard shortcuts. When text recognition found text in one of your photos, a Select text in photo button lays it over the photo there too. New in 1.5.0 A photo sphere has a 360° view button there as well, which shows it as a sphere on the page; opening the viewer shows it flat again. Beside the photo (below it on a phone), the page title is the date the photo was taken, with the time and the place under it. On your own photos the pencil next to the date opens the date editor described under Timestamp. Under the title, labelled buttons hold the photo's actions: Favorite: mark the photo as a favorite, or remove the mark. The button is yellow while it is one. In stars mode it is a wider Rating tile with five stars instead, which work as in the photo viewer (see Rating photos with stars). Share: create a revocable link to this photo, as Share link in the lightbox does (see Revocable Photo Links). The button is green while the photo has a live link. Album: add the photo to one of your albums, or to a new one. Not released yet (comes after 1.6.0) Edit: open the photo editor on this photo. Still photos only. Download: download the original file. When the photo has more than one file (a RAW next to its JPEG, the video of a Live Photo), it opens a list to pick the file from. Not released yet (comes after 1.6.0) On a photo you edited, it always opens the list, with Download edited and Download original first. More: Copy image (still photos, HTTPS only), Rotate 90° counter-clockwise and Rotate 90° clockwise (still photos), Hide photo / Show photo, Archive photo / Unarchive photo, Open in viewer, and Move to trash / Restore from trash. A photo in the trash, hidden or archived says so above these buttons, with a button to restore it, show it again or unarchive it. Then each subject has a card, with the same editors as the details sidebar: People: the faces in the photo. Hovering one marks it on the photo; you can name a face, confirm a suggested name, mark it as not this person, delete it, or mark a face the scan missed with the button at the top of the card. Caption: your caption, with the Things found in the photo under it. Tags: your tags, marked when they came from the file's keywords. Place: the address and a map; the pencil opens Pick location. Place's coordinates line, with the copy button and the altitude, is the same as in the Location section. Camera: the camera and lens, with aperture, shutter speed, focal length (and its 35 mm equivalent) and ISO, the exposure bias, and the same Show more list as the sidebar. File: the file name (it opens the original), its dimensions, megapixels and size (a video's duration and codec), the Category badge, the photo's other formats with a download button each, the folder it is in below your library folder, copies of the file and its stack. Albums and Similar photos, when there are any. Details a photo does not have yet are not listed as empty cards: they are buttons in one Add details card (Add a caption, Add tags, Add a place, Mark a face). Each opens its editor straight away. On a photo someone shared with you, the page shows the photo, its date and the name of its place, Open in viewer and Copy image, and says who shared it. Everything else stays with the owner, as in the lightbox.

New in 1.5.0 Anywhere in the app, press g and then a letter to go to a page. After g, a hint at the bottom of the window lists the letters; it goes away after a moment or on any other key. Keys Page g then p Photos g then l Library g then s Settings g then a Admin area (admins only) g then j My jobs ? The list of keyboard shortcuts The account menu shows the same keys next to its pages, and Keyboard shortcuts in it opens the list. The keys do nothing while you type in a field or while a dialog or the photo viewer is open: the viewer has its own keys, listed below, where g toggles fullscreen.
documents.s: Going to a page with the keyboard

documents.t: Key Action ← / → Previous / Next photo Shift + ← / → Jump back / forward 10 seconds (videos only) Ctrl + ← / → Jump back / forward 1 minute (videos only) Escape Close photo viewer Space Play / pause (videos only) z Toggle zoom (still images only) v Toggle the 360° view (photo spheres only); while it is on, the arrow keys look around and + / - zoom i Toggle sidebar f Toggle favorite (favorites mode) 0 - 5 Set the star rating, 0 clears it (stars mode) h Hide / unhide photo a Archive / unarchive photo p Open the photo's share link dialog e Not released yet (comes after 1.6.0) Open the photo editor (your own still photos) d Move photo to trash g Toggle fullscreen s Start / stop slideshow t Select text in the photo / stop selecting it (only on your own photos where text was recognised) Ctrl + c (⌘ + c on macOS) Copy the photo to the clipboard (still images only; when text is selected, the browser copies the text instead) The f, 0-5, h, a, p and d shortcuts act on the current photo and are disabled on public (unauthenticated) album pages. f does nothing in stars mode and 0-5 do nothing in favorites mode.

Space starts and pauses a video. Holding Shift with the arrow keys jumps ten seconds back or forward, and holding Ctrl instead jumps a full minute — the same split VLC makes between a short and a long jump. The plain arrow keys keep moving between photos even while a video is playing, so skipping through a clip never costs you your place in the album. Each jump is confirmed on screen — the player's own control bar stays hidden when you drive it from the keyboard, so there would otherwise be nothing to see. On macOS, Ctrl with the arrow keys is claimed by Mission Control for switching between desktops, so the one-minute jump may not reach the page there; Shift is unaffected. Seeking is unavailable while a video is still being converted for playback: the first time you play a video your browser cannot play as it is, or any video when you have Always transcode videos turned on in your settings. For as long as that conversion is running the browser is never told how long the video is or how to jump within it, so the player says so rather than ignoring the key.

Not every browser plays every video. H.265 (HEVC), which most phones record in, plays in Safari, and in Chrome and Edge on a machine with a hardware decoder for it, but not in Firefox or in Chrome without one. Older cameras' formats, such as MPEG-2 or Motion JPEG, play nowhere. LibrePhotos asks your browser, for each video, whether it can play it. If it can, you get the original at full resolution. If it cannot, the video is converted to H.264 for you as it plays, capped at 720 lines, and kept for the next time you watch it (see Experimental options for how converted copies are stored). A video your browser says it can play but then fails to decode is converted the same way, automatically. You do not need Always transcode videos for any of this. This applies to you and to anyone you share a video with who signs in. Visitors to a public album without an account are never served a conversion: they get the original, or a copy without its metadata unless every Photo details setting of the link is on. Note New in 1.3.0 On 1.2.1 and older, a video your browser could not play needed Always transcode videos.

Most phones record video in HDR by default: iPhones in Dolby Vision, most Android phones in HLG. Wherever LibrePhotos converts such a video — the gallery thumbnails, and playback whenever it is converted (see Videos your browser cannot play) — it maps the picture down to ordinary SDR colours, so it looks like itself instead of washed out and grey. In the photo grid, an HDR video carries an HDR badge next to its duration. Whether a video is HDR is worked out once, when the scan adds it, together with its codec and pixel format. Videos that were already in your library before this existed are checked by the Probe videos job, which runs by itself after your next scan and rebuilds the thumbnails of the HDR ones, and of any 10-bit or 4:2:2 ones, so thumbnails that looked washed out or did not play are corrected then. See Job System. Note The HDR badge, the scan-time check and Probe videos are new in 1.3.0. 1.2.0 and 1.2.1 already mapped HDR videos to SDR, but could turn bright skies and highlights flat white; older releases converted them washed out.
